## Summary

Implements the first provider-execution layer on top of the canonical payment core in #331. This PR keeps provider-specific behavior behind adapters and capability gates, while adding durable operation/idempotency records and authoritative reconciliation for PlaceToPay and PayPhone.

Depends on #331 and should be reviewed/merged after it.

The generated mobile contract is published separately in diegueins680/TDF-mobile#78 at commit `62dd38cfa0362d0fb880c9f0cd4933693fe77759`.

## What changed

- Adds exact payment-method routing so multi-method checkouts cannot bypass a selected method.
- Separates immutable internal order references from provider merchant references.
- Adds `commerce_provider_operation` for durable create-operation idempotency, resource binding, outcome certainty, encrypted redirect state, and safe ambiguous-result handling.
- Records webhook evidence as either `signature_verified` or `untrusted_callback`; evidence classification is immutable.
- Adds hosted session create/status APIs and provider notification endpoints, including PayPhone's required `/NotificacionPago` compatibility route.
- Implements PlaceToPay SHA-256 notification verification followed by authenticated session lookup.
- Treats PayPhone notifications as untrusted triggers and requires an authenticated Sale lookup before changing canonical payment state.
- Validates provider resource ID, merchant reference, amount, currency, account, environment, checkout, attempt, and intent before reconciliation.
- Prevents fallback after an ambiguous create result, avoiding duplicate cross-provider charges.
- Fails closed for unconfigured PlaceToPay card, bank, or DeUna payment-method identifiers and for unsupported PayPhone methods.
- Extends admin/OpenAPI/generated web and mobile contracts with provider operation and evidence information.
- Adds a reversible migration, production release-manifest registration, schema assertions, regression tests, and an operator verification/runbook document.

## Verification completed

All results below are local/mock/database verification, not provider sandbox or staging evidence.

- `stack test --fast --test-arguments='--match=provider'` — PASS, 76 examples, 0 failures.
- `./scripts/test-provider-execution-runtime-migration.sh` — PASS against PostgreSQL 16, including double apply, encrypted redirect checks, immutable references/evidence, unsigned production callback classification, guarded rollback, operator flag preservation, and reapply.
- `npm run test:production-release` — PASS, 60 tests, 0 failures.
- `npm run generate:api` — PASS and deterministic (`git diff --exit-code`).
- `npm run typecheck:ui` — PASS.
- Mobile `npm run typecheck` — PASS at `62dd38cfa0362d0fb880c9f0cd4933693fe77759`.
- `./scripts/test-automatic-migrations-production-schema.sh` — PASS against an isolated PostgreSQL 17/pgvector database, including manifest verification, backend health, schema verification, second-start idempotency, and unchanged migration checksum.
- `git diff --check` — PASS.

Recorded verification timestamp: 2026-09-14 09:46:43 America/Guayaquil (14:46:43 UTC).

## Migration and rollback

- Forward: `tdf-hq/sql/2026-09-13_provider_execution_runtime.sql`
- Rollback: `tdf-hq/sql/rollback/2026-09-13_provider_execution_runtime_rollback.sql`
- Release manifest ID: `2026-09-13_provider_execution_runtime`
- Rollback intentionally refuses to remove provider operations or untrusted-callback evidence when data exists.
- Provider notification flags are inserted conservatively; rollback removes only rows that still match the migration-owned values/reasons.
- No production data mutation or deployment was performed.

## Configuration and activation

Adapters remain disabled unless the exact environment/account/configuration gates pass. Activation requires, as applicable:

- PlaceToPay login, secret key, process URL, notification URL, and exact method-ID mappings for card, bank, and DeUna.
- PayPhone bearer token, store ID, response URL, approved external-notification registration, and provider account readiness.
- A configured application encryption key for persisted redirect/session material.
- Explicit production account and feature-flag activation after sandbox/staging evidence and operational approval.

## Known blockers and risks

- No PlaceToPay or PayPhone sandbox credentials/contracts were available; no real provider sandbox transaction or callback was executed.
- No configured staging deployment/access was exercised.
- No live transaction, settlement, payout, or production deployment was performed.
- Web/mobile checkout UI does not advertise these methods yet; this PR supplies the backend/runtime and generated contract needed by the dependent UI PR.
- PlaceToPay payment links, recurring mandates, refunds, voids, captures, disputes, settlements, and payouts need separate operation/API work.
- PayPhone's current public notification guide documents no cryptographic signature; callbacks remain untrusted until an authenticated API query confirms the payment.
- A transport-ambiguous create response without a bound provider resource requires manual/provider-console reconciliation; automatic fallback is blocked.
- Mixed taxable/non-taxable basket representation still requires an agreed provider tax-line strategy.
- Marketplace connected-account, split-settlement, and seller-payout flows remain disabled unless provider contract/capability and Ecuadorian legal/accounting review establish a compliant model.

## Review order

1. #331 — canonical core, migrations, audit, architecture, and compatibility.
2. This PR — provider execution, reconciliation, release registration, and generated contracts.
3. Dependent web/mobile checkout and administration PRs.

body:
## Outcome

Completes the safe, provider-neutral payment follow-up on top of merged canonical-core PR #326. This branch keeps every provider disabled until TDF has verified contract, credential, environment, and exact method/capability evidence. It deploys nothing and performs no payment.

## What changed

- binds live payment attempts to canonical intents and synchronizes only authoritative positive lifecycle progress;
- rejects unsupported or unverified routes at attempt creation, including marketplace flows without connected accounts, split settlement, and seller payouts;
- centralizes Datafast, PayPal, and manual-bank runtime availability instead of trusting browser keys or documentation-only catalog rows;
- seeds Datafast, PayPal, PlaceToPay, PayPhone, and manual-bank capability metadata in a disabled/non-routable state;
- fails closed across tickets, courses, bookings, services, Domo quotes, merchandise, and marketplace checkout presentation;
- adds a strict-admin, redacted commerce overview for provider readiness, attempts, refunds, disputes, reconciliation, settlements, commissions, balances, payouts, and audit history;
- refreshes versioned OpenAPI clients and points the mobile submodule to draft TDF-mobile PR #78;
- adds the dated Ecuador provider/method/regulatory matrix, weighted selection, architecture/state diagrams, threat model, ADR, migration/rollback notes, runbooks, blockers, and exact evidence boundary;
- repairs baseline regressions encountered by the complete gates (event-reaction idempotency, onboarding replay/Party isolation, route splitting, and initial bundle budget) without weakening any gate.

## Provider decision

Target minimum portfolio:

1. Datafast — Ecuador cards and issuer/acquirer-approved installments.
2. PayPal Checkout — distinct international wallet; Multiparty remains approval/contract blocked.
3. PlaceToPay — second local failure domain, bank/DeUna redirects, links, and documented delayed-capture operations.
4. PayPhone — distinct wallet/QR/link ecosystem and local fallback.

Kushki is the substitution candidate if PlaceToPay contracting fails. Cash and crypto are research-only. Stripe is not admitted for a direct Ecuador entity. The operational provider set remains **none** until sandbox and contract gates are satisfied.

## Migrations

Additive/reversible scripts registered in the production manifest:

- `2026-09-11_payment_intent_runtime_sync.sql` and rollback;
- `2026-09-11_manual_bank_provider_activation.sql` and rollback (despite the filename, it creates disabled rows and enables nothing);
- `2026-09-11_provider_capability_catalog.sql` and rollback (documentation-only rows, never routable without verified evidence).
- existing `2026-09-09_public_booking_tentative_idempotency.sql` is now registered in the production manifest; its rollback is intentionally non-destructive.

Historical orders, attempts, provider references, ledger/evidence rows, and APIs remain intact. Rollback intentionally refuses to erase financial evidence and requires roll-forward after use. No production migration or data change was performed.

## Verification

Complete local regression evidence on macOS 14.7.7, Node 24.8.0, npm 11.6.0, Stack 3.7.1, and disposable PostgreSQL 16/17 at `2eac48e2b4b0588ad162fe7fd44808b799261567`; subsequent delivery repairs were focused-tested through `ac018a3f1afed8e59c8f7d3c4188ecc01e709e72`:

- `stack test --fast`: 2,544 examples, 0 failures.
- `npm run quality:ui`: lint/typecheck passed; 207/207 suites and 1,870/1,870 tests passed; production build passed; initial-JS budget 378,245/419,840 gzip bytes.
- `npm run quality:mobile`: 68/68 suites and 329/329 tests passed at `c1ae3e34b53f8e709d361677d20b9778bdf87d61`.
- `npm run quality:repo`: passed, including 60/60 production-release and 19/19 CI-pipeline tests; formal audit 0 critical/0 errors.
- `npm run generate:api`: web/mobile generation completed with no drift.
- canonical migration harness on disposable PostgreSQL 16: apply/reapply, constraints, gates, catalog rollback, and evidence-preserving rollback refusal passed.
- full automatic production-schema startup and second idempotent startup passed on disposable PostgreSQL 16; the database was removed afterward.
- refreshed catalog governance passed with zero unreviewed or stale hardcoded-list decisions.
- Login-page unit tests passed 3/3 and the exact Chromium `anonymous RSVP survives signup` persona test passed 1/1.
- authenticated merch HTTP runtime passed 1/1 locally and in GitHub after aligning its fixture with the canonical migration order.
- public-booking automatic migration/replay/resource-concurrency harness passed locally and in GitHub after registering the omitted migration and fixing the disposable PostgreSQL bootstrap wait.

GitHub run [34770799230](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/34770799230) and associated checks passed 17/17 at `ac018a3f1afed8e59c8f7d3c4188ecc01e709e72`. Intermediate failures and their exact repairs are retained in the research/test record; this is hosted CI evidence, not provider sandbox evidence.

Final documentation-only head verification: GitHub run [34774800412](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/34774800412) completed successfully at `49b1a5f2e83e32850f2977cfdede9eb6bc5c4c0c` on 2026-09-13 18:45:13 UTC, with all 17 PR checks green. Its first persona-browser attempt reported one transient Chromium-desktop contrast sample (4.32:1 versus the 4.5:1 threshold) while 45 journeys passed and 10 were intentionally skipped; a controlled rerun of the unchanged commit passed all 56 configured persona journeys and the aggregate quality gate. No code was changed to conceal or bypass the observed attempt.

Warnings were non-fatal and are disclosed in the research record. These are local/mock/disposable-database results—not provider sandbox evidence.

## Dependencies and review order

1. Merged parent core PR #326 is the base already present in `main`.
2. Review TDF-mobile #64, then stacked payment PR [TDF-mobile #78](https://github.com/diegueins680/TDF-mobile/pull/78). PR #78 supersedes stale generated-only mobile PR #76.
3. Review this parent completion PR; its submodule pointer references mobile #78.
4. Open separate provider-evidence/activation PRs only after the relevant contracts, credentials, webhook registration, and credentialed sandbox matrix exist.

## Blocked before activation

- Datafast merchant/acquirer agreement, sandbox entity/authorization material, exact entitlement matrix, registered URLs, and certification evidence.
- PayPal sandbox app/accounts/webhook ID and Multiparty/subscription approvals.
- PlaceToPay Ecuador contract/login/secret plus completion of the shared executor/return/notification path.
- PayPhone business agreement/token/store/test users plus completion of the shared executor and authoritative notification/status behavior.
- authorized staging session and provider secrets; none were available.
- qualified Ecuador legal/accounting/privacy and PCI-scope review, especially for marketplace custody, invoicing, tax, seller liability, recurring consent, and payouts.

No provider sandbox, staging test/deploy, production deploy, live transaction, screenshot, refund, or payout was performed. No secret values were accessed or placed in code/logs/PR text.

## Documentation

- `docs/payments/ecuador-payment-platform-audit-2026-09-11.md`

---

## CI reconciliation follow-up — September 15, 2026

This updates the earlier CI audit; it does not change the payment-provider activation boundary.

- Initial audit main: `17a33eca11d585d84435af85340beece9b51d14e`.
- Current main: `73edd77a36c8dcc73e5217303c62376ae684853b`.
- Original correction PR [#333](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/pull/333), final SHA `5bceb329f034cdfadf077f8f2889aa50bd402c7c`, was merged by another actor/account `diegueins680` at 2026-09-15 04:11:04 UTC. This agent did not merge or enable auto-merge.
- Initially open PR [#331](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/pull/331): initial head `49b1a5f2e83e32850f2977cfdede9eb6bc5c4c0c`; final evaluated/pushed head `25416b43eb8a24b2a57a180fbb846d9db8addcb1`. It is open, draft, mergeable/conflict-free, with auto-merge off. Its 17 reported checks are successful. It still requires a fresh human approval and the author's draft/readiness decision.
- Latest inventory: 36 open PRs; only #331 was present in the initial scope. Later PRs were not rewritten.

### Before / after evidence

| Workflow/check | Before | Current main | Final PR #331 SHA |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CI: changes, repo-quality, ui-quality, mobile-quality, backend-quality, persona-web-e2e, api-contract-tests, migration-tests, api-contracts, production-migrations, quality | Original deterministic migration, generated-client, Haskell, UI and preview defects; aggregate failures were downstream. | All jobs successful through [Build Image's reusable CI](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/34927839148). | All 11 jobs successful in [fresh CI](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/34937258694). |

No deployment performed. |

Prior correction and fresh main execution cover the enrichment fix. |

[Last correction-SHA check FAILED](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/34922343353): Meta debugger HTTP 400 / API code 2 after bounded retries. External/account-configuration blocker remains. |

A later read-only experiment on another actor's branch is outside this evaluated SHA. |
| Cloudflare Pages, Vercel, Vercel Preview Comments | External deployment status, outside GitHub Actions implementation scope. | Not substituted for application CI. | All 3 reported statuses successful in PR rollup. |

### Integration root causes and changes

Main's merge made #331 conflict with the corrected baseline. The resolution preserves reaction locking/privacy/legacy evidence, durable per-party onboarding recovery above public routes, payment-provider fail-closed controls, and lazy route/analytics splitting.

The authoritative migration manifest's automatic merge duplicated two entries and omitted contextual reputation. A uniqueness regression reproduced 104 unique IDs in 106 entries. The corrected manifest contains the exact 102 ordered main entries plus three payment migrations: 105 total, with no changed SQL or historical checksums. Three additional prerequisite-order assertions protect reputation, payment-intent synchronization and provider capability setup.

While integration was being validated, another actor pushed equivalent application/migration reconciliation in `e39abf5a4ce2151e03dbd91051ba508295081efb`. Our first normal push was safely rejected. We compared the resulting trees, retained that published commit, and appended only:
- `scripts/__tests__/production-release.test.mjs`: three migration-order assertions.
- `tdf-hq-ui/src/pages/LoginPage.test.tsx`: explicitly advance the real MUI dialog exit timers inside awaited React act, restoring real timers afterward; retain the assertion that the dialog is absent.

This fixes the dismissal test's wall-clock animation race without increasing timeouts, changing application behavior or reducing coverage. No force-push or contributor-history rewrite occurred.

Generated clients remain authoritative and reproducible in both consumers: SHA-256 `c77b987df160bab0c719a17b850a8df27f5da3bab9decabe8772a84b8644bc4a`. Existing mobile commit `c1ae3e34b53f8e709d361677d20b9778bdf87d61` is retained; no additional mobile commit was needed. ### Validation and honest local limitations

- Fresh final-SHA CI: UI 207 suites / 1,971 tests; mobile 68 / 329; backend 2,546 examples / zero failures; persona 46 passed / 10 legitimate deduplication skips. All contract, migration, runtime, dependency/security-policy, lint, type, build and aggregate gates passed. The separately dispatched final-SHA image workflow also passed every job.

- Final-SHA repetition of that complete local command exited 1: repo checks, UI lint/types passed; UI 202 suites / 1,964 tests passed and 5 suites / 7 tests failed in 2,012.9 seconds. Failures begin with unchanged five-second watchdogs in MerchAdminPage, ArtistPublicPage, publicRoutes and ForbiddenPage, plus a MarketplaceOrderTracking loading-state cascade. Host memory pressure was directly observed. No process was terminated and no test limit was increased. This repetition is not green and the later local build/mobile/backend stages did not execute.
- One isolated diagnostic run of those five files passed all 5 suites / 14 tests in 17.98 seconds, without any source, timeout or assertion change. This supports the resource-contention diagnosis, not a reclassification of the failed complete run. No repeated full-suite rerun-to-green was used.
- Final image digest: `sha256:8ca18af9208eea1d6b646c933ecfd887f5230e1353d870b8aaaf082a2225882b`, published only under the immutable final commit tag.
- Final focused production-release tests: 53 passed; strict catalog audit exited 0 for all 1,111 candidates; generated clients show no drift; `git diff --check` passed and the worktree is clean.
- Separate final-SHA `npm run build --workspace=tdf-hq-ui` exited 0: production build and unchanged initial-bundle gate passed (5 preloads / 314,737 gzip bytes). The pre-existing large-chunk warning remains disclosed; no limit was raised.
- Separate final-SHA `REQUIRE_MOBILE_WORKSPACE=1 npm exec --offline --yes --package=node@22.14.0 -- npm run quality:mobile` exited 0: lint, types, 68 suites / 329 tests passed (50.507 seconds for tests).
- Separate final-SHA `REQUIRE_STACK=1 npm exec --offline --yes --package=node@22.14.0 -- npm run quality:backend` exited 0: 2,546 examples, zero failures (8.3815 seconds for tests).
- Docker migration harness could not start its disposable PostgreSQL service within its startup window, before any SQL assertion. A native PostgreSQL 16.10 equivalent preserved the original assertion body verbatim, replacing only isolated database setup/psql adapters; it passed apply/reapply, disabled-provider defaults, invalid-activation rejection, intent binding, immutable references, balanced commissions, dual-control payout and evidence-preserving rollback refusal. Its own temporary database was cleaned up. The failed Docker startup is not reported as a passed Docker run.

### Expected skips, security and rollback

The 10 persona skips deduplicate mutation-heavy journeys across browser projects. Ordinary PR CI does not publish the backend executable; its upload step is legitimately skipped. Build Image requests the artifact and successfully uploads/downloads it. Manual enrichment uses the non-publishing dry-run branch and skips its mutually exclusive scheduled branch. Success-only runs omit failure notifications. Datadog's missing-key fallback skips because the real test step executes. No unexpected job skips occurred in final CI or image build.

Datadog is verified as TDF Records / US1. Existing repository `DD_API_KEY` and `DD_APP_KEY` are configured; no secret values were read, copied or rotated by this agent. Its two production endpoint tests verify deployed liveness, not this PR's deployment or actual database connectivity. No paid plan or recurring test schedule was enabled.

The published follow-up is test-only. Existing additive payment migrations keep providers disabled. No provider activation, credential rotation, live transaction, production migration or deployment was performed. Historical ledger/checksum/evidence rows remain immutable; rollback must refuse erasure after financial evidence exists and use a reviewed roll-forward instead. Existing dependency advisory exceptions remain unchanged; passing the repository security policy is not a zero-advisory claim.

### Remaining actions / status boundary

1. **Meta blocker:** workflow Refresh Instagram Token, step Check/Refresh Token, repository-scoped `FACEBOOK_APP_ID`/`FACEBOOK_APP_SECRET` (parent debugger) and separate `INSTAGRAM_APP_ID`/`INSTAGRAM_APP_SECRET`/`INSTAGRAM_ACCESS_TOKEN`. Account access works; debug_token returns HTTP 400 / code 2, service temporarily unavailable. A platform-wide outage is not proven. The app administrator must verify the TDF Bot / TDF Bot-IG inspector association and investigate with Meta if needed; do not blindly rotate keys. Then use existing `action=check` and require account, ownership and expiry validation to succeed. Optional `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` is absent; notification omission does not hide the primary failure.
2. **Local environment:** complete a final-SHA full local suite in an adequately resourced environment. Fresh hosted CI and image build are green, but the final local repetition is not.
3. **Human review:** #331 remains draft with no effective fresh approval; the repository requires one approval and dismisses stale reviews. No protections, draft state, approvals or merge controls were bypassed.
4. **Original handoff:** #333 cannot be delivered as an open correction PR because another actor already merged it. Its fixes are now on main; this approved continuation repaired the originally scoped #331 without creating an extra correction PR.

Verified final PR CI/image results, current-main workflow results, older-SHA scheduled evidence, local limitations and the Meta blocker are deliberately distinguished. The repository-wide objective is not claimed fully green.



---

## Updated Instagram blocker — verified Meta response (September 15, 2026)

This supersedes the earlier uncertainty between an outage and inspector configuration.

The attached browser shows a response from Meta Support in [case 1978991836117141](https://developers.facebook.com/support/bugs/1978991836117141/). Meta states that Facebook Graph `/debug_token` does not reliably support Instagram Login tokens, including dashboard-generated tokens; changing the authenticating app/credential combination will not resolve that limitation. Meta reports no documented read-only API with equivalent introspection and recommends its [Access Token Debugger portal](https://developers.facebook.com/tools/debug/accesstoken/) for manual inspection. The case is marked closed. This is Meta's stated limitation, not proof of a platform-wide outage.

Consequently, the existing failure is classified as an **unsupported provider validation path**. Repository secret-name/update metadata is unchanged; no credential value was accessed. The original run remains failed: [34922343353](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/34922343353). It was not rerun, and its ownership/expiry gate was not removed or treated as successful based only on `/me`.

Next step requires an explicitly approved validation/lifecycle design: inspect the current credential privately through Meta's portal, or authorize a supported reauthorization/exchange/refresh workflow with securely bound provenance and provider-returned lifecycle evidence. A working-account response alone cannot replace ownership and expiry validation. No token refresh, reauthorization, secret replacement, deployment, new attestation, or weaker check was performed.

GitHub access and the repository preflight were reverified; preflight has no errors (only absent daily memory notes). Main remains `73edd77a36c8dcc73e5217303c62376ae684853b`. PR #331 remains `25416b43eb8a24b2a57a180fbb846d9db8addcb1`, open/draft/mergeable with 17 successful checks and no auto-merge. The earlier full-local UI failure and human-review requirements remain disclosed.

## Summary

- adds a provider-neutral adapter contract using integer minor units and no raw card-data fields
- implements disabled PlaceToPay Ecuador WebCheckout create/query/cancel and signed-notification verification
- implements disabled PayPhone API Sale create/query/cancel/same-day reversal with authoritative-query enforcement
- persists exact method-capability evidence and prevents cross-method capability escalation
- redacts existing Datafast/legacy PayPal credentials and adds an allowlisted, no-redirect provider transport

## Dependency and merge order

Draft and stacked on #326. Merge #326 first, then rebase/merge this PR. All new provider accounts and capabilities remain disabled.

## Evidence

- `stack test --test-arguments=--match=provider --fast`: 69 examples, 0 failures
- `stack test --fast`: 2,506 examples, 0 failures (before the transport-only follow-up; transport was compiled and covered by the focused suite)

- `npm run audit:catalog-lists`: passed after reviewed technical-enum classification
- automatic production-schema migration verifier: passed and idempotent on disposable PostgreSQL 16

These are local/mock/contract tests only. No Datafast, PayPal, PlaceToPay, or PayPhone sandbox transaction was executed.

## Security and activation

- fixed HTTPS provider hosts, redirects disabled, 15-second timeout, 1 MiB response limit
- PlaceToPay signatures are verified but still require authenticated session reconciliation
- PayPhone browser callbacks are never authoritative and always require authenticated query
- request bodies, buyer input, nonces, tokens, and derived auth are not printable through ordinary log summaries
- no PAN, CVV, magnetic-stripe data, or invented credentials

Activation requires merchant contracts, per-environment credentials, exact method/capability evidence, webhook/return registration, credentialed sandbox evidence, and separate legal/accounting/PCI review. Required staging secret names are documented in the runbook.

## Remaining in this draft

- canonical runtime API wiring and persistent attempt/event transitions
- credentialed provider sandbox tests (blocked by accounts/secrets/contracts)
- UI activation (belongs to the dependent checkout PR)

title: fix: document mobile onboarding feed retry
body:
# Onboarding mobile feed retry — 2026-09-10

## Outcome

The mobile onboarding treatment now gives users a direct, localized retry action when its events or moments feed fails while the device remains online. The action refreshes only active React Query entries under the authenticated Party's onboarding cache key, so recovery does not require leaving the focused first-value experience.

User-triggered recovery exposes an accessible busy and disabled state while the request is active. Repeated taps, reconnects, and foreground events share the same in-flight Party request; automatic lifecycle recovery remains visually silent. Completion restores the retry action even when the refetch rejects, allowing another attempt without remounting the gate.

## Verification

- The focused onboarding-gate Jest suite passed: 1 suite, 30 tests.
- The complete mobile Jest corpus passed: 70 suites, 437 tests.
- Mobile TypeScript passed.
- Strict mobile ESLint passed with zero warnings.

title: fix(domo): verify safe fallback booking journey
body:
# Draft PR: make the Domo fallback accurate, accessible, and browser-verified

## Problem

The public Domo route had no runtime test for its no-authoritative-quote booking fallback. Current browser inspection found that it defaulted a local Ecuador date-time to UTC, lacked contact autocomplete metadata, failed minimum contrast at 20 rendered nodes, and autoplayed/preloaded its hero video without a control.

These defects sit on a public revenue-onboarding path: a visitor could send a request five hours early, face unnecessary data entry effort, struggle to read route content, and incur motion/media transfer before choosing it.

## Changes

- Default the fixed-location fallback to `America/Guayaquil` when no Domo-specific timezone is configured.
- Preserve the same manual-booking payload and idempotency key across an ambiguous retry.
- Add `name`, `email`, and `tel` autocomplete semantics.
- Introduce contrast-safe light/dark foreground variants while retaining Domo brand accents.
- Make hero media poster-first: no autoplay, `preload="none"`, and a visible 44px play/pause control.
- Add a real-browser synthetic Domo journey on desktop, phone, and tablet covering:
  - `503` then successful retry;
  - exact Ecuador-to-UTC conversion;
  - identical request/key reuse;
  - truthful no-hold/no-payment states;
  - keyboard submit and pointer retry;
  - autocomplete, target size, and 320px reflow;
  - zero video request before opt-in and media-control transitions;
  - axe serious/critical scans across all four route themes;
  - final screenshots.
- Add focused unit coverage and richer axe-node diagnostics.

## Evidence

- Pre-fix timezone regression: expected `2030-01-15T15:00:00Z`, received `2030-01-15T10:00:00Z`.
- Pre-fix autocomplete regression: expected `name`, received `null`.
- Pre-fix axe run: one serious contrast rule affecting 20 nodes, with ratios as low as 1.58:1.
- Pre-fix media regression: `Reproducir fondo` control absent.
- Final focused Jest: 1 suite / 3 tests passed.
- Final focused Domo Playwright: 3/3 passed on Chromium desktop/phone/tablet.
- Final complete Playwright: 38 passed / 4 configured skips.
- UI lint: 0 errors / 102 existing warnings.
- TypeScript + production build: passed; 12,415 modules; 413,021 gzip bytes initial JS.
- Repository quality, catalog unit test, and strict catalog audit: passed.
- Full `quality:ui`: not green—185/186 suites passed, but one baseline-identical 24,000-line course-registration suite hit its five-second timeout and cascaded to 168 failures. Domo passed inside the run; isolated reproduction confirms the timing defect.

Detailed findings, coverage, evidence boundaries, screenshots, and deferred acceptance criteria: `reports/domo-fallback-browser-audit-2026-09-10.md`.

## Risks and compatibility

- No business rule, price, payment, availability, API, schema, backend, generated client, role, permission, mobile pointer, analytics, or dependency change.
- The venue remains fully understandable from the poster; visitors must now opt in to motion. If media playback fails, the poster remains but dedicated failure feedback is deferred.
- Contrast values are route-scoped; brand accents remain for identity and actions.
- Browser responses are synthetic interceptions. PR #324 separately verifies the compiled booking handler and PostgreSQL integrity; this PR does not claim one combined end-to-end stack.
- Domo runtime coverage is Chromium-only; the broader critical Firefox/WebKit subset passed but does not include this route.

## Rollback

Revert this branch's commits. No database or generated-client rollback is required. Reverting would restore the five-hour fallback risk, inaccessible contrast, and unsolicited hero media, so keep the new regression tests if the implementation is replaced.

## Remaining gaps

- Connect the browser journey to the real compiled handler and disposable PostgreSQL.
- Verify actual media decoding/failure, screen readers, 200% zoom, physical touch, orientation, and virtual-keyboard behavior.
- Add Domo Firefox/WebKit coverage and interruption/offline continuity.
- Exercise an approved sandbox authoritative-quote provider.
- Establish consented funnel and field Web Vitals measurement; no uplift is claimed.
- Refactor the baseline course-registration timing defect so `quality:ui` is fully green without increasing timeouts.

No merge or production deployment is requested.

title: fix: make public booking replays authoritative
body:
# Draft PR: make public booking replays authoritative

## Problem

The preceding idempotency implementation checked resource availability before acquiring the per-key lock and reading the durable replay receipt. Once the first booking committed, its own room allocation caused a later identical retry to return `409` instead of the original booking. Changed input under the same key could likewise surface a generic availability conflict instead of the stable idempotency conflict.

The earlier browser test mocked HTTP and could not observe this database-dependent ordering defect.

## Changes

- Move public-booking resource resolution into the key-serialized database transaction.
- Return a matching durable receipt before consulting mutable room availability.
- Retain validation, deterministic resource locking, exclusion-constraint conflict handling, transactional writes, and engineer-notification suppression.
- Add a guarded real HTTP/PostgreSQL concurrency harness that:
  - builds a production-like schema using the reviewed migration path;
  - launches the exact tested backend executable with a clean provider-free environment;
  - observes an advisory-lock waiter for concurrent equal-key requests;
  - verifies post-commit replay and changed-payload conflict semantics;
  - verifies concurrent different-key resource conflict;
  - asserts booking, Party, receipt, resource, allocation, credential, and role cardinality.
- Run the harness in backend CI and ensure future harness-only changes select backend validation.

## Evidence

- Pre-fix real runtime: failed with `Post-commit equal-key replay response: expected '200', got '409'`.
- Final HTTP/PostgreSQL test: passed with equal-key `200/200`, post-commit replay `200`, changed-payload `409`, and overlapping resource `200/409`.
- Focused Hspec: 1 example / 0 failures after production/test executable rebuild.
- CI pipeline contract: 18/18 tests passed.
- Catalog test: 1/1 passed; strict catalog audit passed.
- Shell syntax and diff checks passed.

Detailed evidence and coverage: `reports/public-booking-http-concurrency-audit-2026-09-09.md`.

## Risks and compatibility

- No API, schema, generated client, UI, mobile, dependency, price, policy, permission, role, or payment behavior changes.
- A genuinely new request holds its key transaction while resolving resources; matching replays now skip availability queries. The key lock affects only equal idempotency keys.
- The two-second trigger exists only in the disposable test database.
- The integration script refuses non-test/non-loopback targets and starts the server with `env -i` so inherited provider credentials are unavailable.

## Rollback

Revert this branch's commits. No database rollback is required. Reverting would restore the incorrect post-commit replay ordering, so retain the HTTP regression if the handler implementation is replaced.

## Remaining gaps

- Inventory external clients before enforcing the required header in rollout.
- Exercise the Domo fallback at runtime.
- Add crash-after-commit fault injection and local notification-sink verification.
- Staging, production, analytics, screen-reader, physical-device, and field-performance validation remain out of scope for this batch.

No merge or production deployment is requested.

title: fix: make public tentative bookings idempotent
body:
# Draft PR: make public tentative bookings idempotent and conflict-safe

## Problem

The unauthenticated no-price booking compatibility route had no durable idempotency contract. A retry after a timeout or dropped response could create another tentative booking. PostgreSQL already prevented overlapping resource allocations, but the handler did not translate its `23P01` exclusion failure into the documented `409` response.

## Changes

- Require and validate `Idempotency-Key` for `POST /bookings/public`.
- Add an additive PII-free replay table containing only key, normalized-request SHA-256, booking reference, and timestamp.
- Serialize equal keys, replay equal payloads, reject changed payloads with `409`, and avoid duplicate engineer notification.
- Run guest Party creation, booking/resource writes, and replay receipt in one transaction.
- Map the existing allocation exclusion failure to `409` after rollback.
- Preserve payload-scoped keys across ordinary retry and same-tab reload/back using a sessionStorage name derived only from a Web Crypto SHA-256 digest.
- Update both known first-party callers, OpenAPI, generated web/mobile types, production migration manifest, CI migration rehearsal, Jest, Hspec/build evidence, and desktop/phone Playwright retry coverage.
- Repair one pre-existing migration-manifest ancestry pointer to the byte-identical introducing commit in current history so the guarded local release planner can evaluate the stack.

## Evidence

- Audit: `reports/public-booking-idempotency-conflict-audit-2026-09-09.md`
- Focused web Jest: 3 suites / 28 tests passed.
- Focused web ESLint, web TypeScript, mobile lint, and mobile TypeScript passed.
- UI production build passed; bundle guard: 5 preloads / 413,015 gzip bytes initial JavaScript.
- Backend focused Hspec: `PublicBookingReq` 3/3 and `ensurePartyRecord` 1/1 passed; production and 184-module test executable compiled/linked.
- New PostgreSQL 17 idempotency migration rehearsal passed.
- Existing PostgreSQL 17 service-booking rehearsal passed and rejected an overlapping legacy allocation.
- Production-release suite passed 49/49.
- The guarded release planner passed in non-mutating dry-run mode with an empty command list after repairing the pre-existing manifest ancestry pointer.
- The strict catalog-list gate initially found two new fingerprints and one stale fingerprint; the reviewed metadata was updated, and the exact local discovery/policy commands now pass.
- Playwright retry journey passed 2/2 on desktop and phone; the first synthetic `503` and second successful POST used the exact same key.
- Mobile contract commit `57abd23c0522133274e5bc2aa1a7e524d94dd62b` is available on its pushed feature branch.
- Mobile draft PR: https://github.com/diegueins680/TDF-mobile/pull/71.

## Risks and compatibility

- The endpoint now requires a 16–128 character visible-ASCII key. Known generated and first-party clients are updated; unknown external consumers were not inventoried and will receive documented `400` until migrated.
- Browser storage is only a key-continuity aid. Server/database state is authoritative, and no contact payload is stored in the browser key name or replay table.
- Exact handler behavior was compiled and source-reviewed but not invoked through a configured PostgreSQL-backed HTTP process. Migration invariants and the client retry are verified independently.
- No price, payment, cancellation, role, permission, feature flag, customer message, analytics payload, or production data changed.
- No conversion, Web Vitals, provider, SMTP, staging, or production claim is made.

## Migration and rollback

Apply `tdf-hq/sql/2026-09-09_public_booking_tentative_idempotency.sql` through the reviewed production manifest before serving this code. It is additive and idempotent.

The supplied rollback intentionally retains the replay table. Older application code ignores it; deleting it would allow a historical retry key to create a duplicate booking. Roll back application traffic first and define any later retention/drop policy separately.

## Remaining gaps

- Add a barrier-synchronized PostgreSQL-backed HTTP integration for equal retry, changed payload, and overlapping resource requests.
- Inventory external callers before rollout.
- Add privacy-reviewed exactly-once booking funnel measurement.
- Runtime-exercise the Domo legacy fallback retry.
- Complete screen-reader, keyboard/focus, zoom, offline, and physical-device validation.

No merge or deployment is requested by this draft.

title: fix: keep public bookings guest-safe and truthful
body:
# Draft PR: truthful guest booking identity and return continuity

## Problem

The no-quote public-booking compatibility endpoint silently created a credential with a random password, assigned automatic customer access, discarded the generated credentials, and sent no customer message. The public form nevertheless promised automatic account access and email confirmation. Optional login/signup links also discarded the selected service, campaign query, and hash.

## Changes

- Reuse the established guest-commerce `ensurePartyRecord` path for legacy tentative bookings, leaving explicit account creation to signup.
- Preserve the exact safe public-booking path, query, and hash in optional login and signup links through the shared redirect sanitizer.
- Replace unsupported email/account promises with truthful guest-booking, returned-ID, and existing WhatsApp recovery guidance.
- Add a SQLite guest-identity regression, focused router/copy assertions, and desktop/Pixel 7 Playwright coverage with screenshots and axe checks.
- Add the dated audit with capability, coverage, historical revalidation, evidence limits, and prioritized transaction-integrity/measurement backlog.

## Evidence

- Audit: `reports/public-booking-guest-continuity-audit-2026-09-09.md`
- Focused public-booking Jest initially passed 1 suite / 12 tests; after the final one-label refinement, resource-starved retries timed out and cascaded through React `act()` scopes. No source timeout/assertion was weakened; a clean final Jest rerun remains required in CI.
- UI TypeScript and focused ESLint passed.
- UI production build passed; bundle guard reported 5 preloads / 413,022 gzip bytes initial JavaScript.
- Final public-booking Playwright: 2/2 passed on Chromium desktop and Pixel 7 emulation using synthetic HTTP fixtures and an extended command-line timeout under machine load; assertions were unchanged and real final screenshots were captured.
- Focused backend Hspec: 1 example / 0 failures using isolated SQLite.

## Risks and boundaries

- No schema, OpenAPI response, price, policy, role, permission, payment, feature flag, dependency, mobile pointer, or production state changes.
- The browser run mocks the backend and does not prove PostgreSQL, SMTP, provider, staging, or production behavior.
- The legacy route still lacks durable server idempotency and an atomic exclusion-backed hold. Those require a reviewed contract/migration and are the highest-priority next batch.
- Booking funnel analytics are not yet implemented; no conversion uplift is claimed.
- Public-booking copy remains in the route's existing hardcoded Spanish structure; full Spanish/English catalog migration is deferred.

## Rollback

Revert this focused commit. Do not restore undisclosed credential creation as a long-term behavior; if compatibility requires temporary UI rollback, retain the guest-only backend identity invariant.

## Remaining gaps

- PostgreSQL HTTP/integration and concurrent retry/conflict coverage.
- Durable legacy-route idempotency and serialized resource exclusion.
- Privacy-reviewed booking funnel events and real baseline.
- Real auth round-trip, SMTP/provider sandbox, keyboard/screen-reader, enlarged-text, and physical-device validation.

No merge or deployment is requested by this draft.

Endurece el release lane para una activación futura sin activar reputación contextual. `CONTEXTUAL_REPUTATION_ENABLED=false` permanece fijado tanto en staging como en producción hasta que G0 tenga evidencia aprobada; producción además requiere una cohorte piloto aplicada por el servidor.

Este PR no despliega, no activa el flujo y no abre la compuerta DB. La activación de staging requiere primero la decisión G0 y su evidencia; la activación de producción requiere además una cohorte server-side. El worker queda para un rollout posterior e independiente.

title: fix: reconcile onboarding from server evidence
body:
# Draft PR: Reconcile onboarding across devices from server evidence

## Problem

A real first useful action could succeed on device A while its separate onboarding handshake was lost. Same-device mobile retry was already durable, but device B had no local action label and could not reconcile the Party's existing server evidence. The legacy completion endpoint also persisted whichever evidenced category the client submitted first, so later requests could misattribute an earlier action.

## Changes

- add authenticated `POST /session/onboarding/reconcile` with no request body or client-selected Party/action
- infer the earliest Party-bound supported action inside the signup window across artist follow, access request, event save, and moment reaction evidence
- document deterministic exact-time tie order without using intent as authority
- route legacy `/session/onboarding/complete` through the same server inference so evidence wins over a hint or explicit exit
- retain the atomic incomplete-to-complete compare-and-set and existing response shape
- reconcile web onboarding after authenticated cookie bootstrap or bearer-token login
- reconcile mobile on authenticated hydration, reconnect, and foreground
- coalesce overlapping same-session mobile triggers and serialize a direct completion behind in-flight reconciliation
- discard stale Party-A results after a Party-B switch
- clear mobile retry metadata only when `completedAt` proves durable completion
- emit onboarding analytics only for `newlyCompleted=true` and the canonical non-null server-returned value
- prevent the paused onboarding experiment from claiming conversion when another action was actually first
- update the canonical OpenAPI contract and regenerate web/mobile clients with the mobile workspace required

## Evidence and tests

- canonical API generation with `REQUIRE_MOBILE_WORKSPACE=1`: passed for web and mobile
- backend exact cross-device Hspec: 1 example / 0 failures
- backend onboarding Hspec match: 3 examples / 0 failures
- backend evidence Hspec match: 21 examples / 0 failures
- final full mobile Jest: 67 suites / 393 tests
- final mobile typecheck and zero-warning lint: passed
- mobile production-profile release check: passed, including five release assets, typecheck/lint, identity/config validation, and public Expo config
- focused web API/analytics/session reconciliation Jest: 4 suites / 19 tests
- web TypeScript: passed after correcting one strict-null issue found by the first run
- web production build and focused zero-warning lint: passed
- full serial web Jest: 185/186 suites and 1,593/1,761 tests passed; all 168 failures were confined to unchanged `CourseRegistrationsAdminPage.test.tsx` after its first timeout
- repository quality and strict catalog audit: passed; detailed component results and advisory findings are recorded in `reports/onboarding-cross-device-reconciliation-audit-2026-09-09.md`
- initial multi-word Hspec match attempts were command-shape failures and ran zero examples; they are not presented as product test failures or passes
- no native-device, PostgreSQL/staging, production, or field-analytics validation was performed

## Security, privacy, and authority

The endpoint derives Party identity only from the authenticated session and accepts no body. It cannot assign roles/modules, accept product intent as permission, or disclose domain evidence. Clients retain existing auth binding/generation guards and do not store or emit tokens, emails, phone numbers, comments, captions, object IDs, or other free text.

## Risk and rollback

Risk is concentrated in evidence-query cost and completion/analytics timing. The event-save audit path currently decodes all matching Party save timestamps to preserve SQLite/PostgreSQL correctness; this should be bounded after real query-plan evidence. Analytics remains intentionally at-most-once: a response lost after commit can undercount without duplicating events. No schema migration or new dependency is included.

Rollback consists of the focused root commit and mobile submodule commit. Existing clients remain compatible because `/complete` and the response schema are preserved; new clients against an old server fail the new reconciliation POST closed.

## Remaining gaps

- real PostgreSQL handler/query-plan validation
- synthetic two-device staging walkthrough and analytics ingestion inspection
- iOS/Android offline, foreground, account-switch, enlarged-text, and screen-reader checks
- durable deduplicated analytics receipt if lossless measurement is required
- stacked-branch reconciliation with current root/mobile `main` before merge
- next broader audit batch: service booking and checkout journeys

Detailed evidence: `reports/onboarding-cross-device-reconciliation-audit-2026-09-09.md`.

Root and mobile branch: `feature/onboarding-cross-device-reconciliation-20260909`.

Local implementation commits: root `08dacddc0f6eab7e50e94dff3272df491380c6a9`; mobile `f487de478939b3c19a62b5f54aa876d96a4eb32c`.

The mobile commit was published before the root submodule pointer. Draft reviews: root https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/pull/302 and mobile https://github.com/diegueins680/TDF-mobile/pull/61. The stack is behind current `origin/main` in both repositories and must be reconciled and fully revalidated before merge. Do not merge or deploy this stacked batch independently of its base.

title: Fix interrupted onboarding completion recovery
body:
# Draft PR: Recover interrupted onboarding completion safely

## Problem

A first useful action could succeed on the server while the separate onboarding-completion request failed. Mobile swallowed that failure and had no Party-bound retry after relaunch. The server also rejected a later retry solely because the handshake arrived after the 24-hour window, even when the durable action evidence was created in time.

## Changes

- persist only an allowlisted first-value retry label under the authenticated Party
- require and assert the initiating auth session across persistence, request, cleanup, state, and analytics
- retry once on authenticated bootstrap, app foreground, and offline-to-online recovery
- keep completion analytics gated by the server's atomic `newlyCompleted` result
- prevent an older eligibility GET from overwriting a newer completion
- accept delayed first-value handshakes when durable evidence is in the signup window
- preserve evidence time in `firstValueCompletedAt` and handshake time in `completedAt` for newly accepted completions; legacy rows are left unchanged
- keep late explicit exits, missing evidence, and out-of-window evidence rejected
- update canonical OpenAPI documentation and regenerate both clients
- keep `single-feature-onboarding-v1` disabled

## Evidence and tests

- mobile focused recovery: 2 suites / 24 tests passed
- mobile focused onboarding surfaces: 5 suites / 47 tests passed
- mobile full Jest: 67 suites / 386 tests passed on the final serial rerun
- mobile typecheck, lint, and release checks passed
- focused web session/onboarding/routing: 3 suites / 22 tests passed
- web typecheck passed
- canonical API generation passed with required mobile workspace
- repository doctor exited 0 with 14 OK / 4 documented warnings / 0 errors
- backend late-reconciliation match: 3 examples / 0 failures
- backend evidence match: 20 examples / 0 failures after correcting a SQLite/PostgreSQL timestamp-comparison regression caught by the first run
- full web lint did not complete under local resource contention; generated types are lint-ignored, while hosted `ui-quality` passed its configured UI lint, type, test, and build sequence
- every selected hosted root check passed on implementation commit `ba19476b984f4b63ee93be8c8b8efb50aa36272c`, including API contracts, backend, build, repository, mobile, persona web E2E, UI, hardcoded-list, and production-migration gates; workflow-classified `migration-tests` was skipped
- Vercel and Cloudflare preview checks passed; no production deployment was run

Detailed evidence: `reports/onboarding-completion-recovery-audit-2026-09-08.md`.

## Risk and rollback

Risk is concentrated in onboarding timestamp semantics and mobile provider lifecycle. No schema or response-shape migration is required. The backend still derives Party identity from the session and requires durable in-window evidence. Mobile persistence is only a retry hint and cannot grant eligibility, roles, modules, or permissions.

Rollback is the focused root commit plus the mobile submodule-pointer commit. A stale client marker is harmless: the idempotent server response returns `newlyCompleted=false` and cleanup is best-effort.

## Remaining gaps

- pending retry metadata does not transfer across devices; server-side reconciliation is the next integrity batch
- analytics is intentionally at-most-once and may undercount when the server commits but its response is lost
- native device and authenticated staging walkthroughs were not available
- no screenshots were created because rendered UI did not change
- broader platform audit and localization backlog remains in the report

This is a stacked draft PR based on the preceding onboarding recovery/localization work. It must not be merged before its base stack.

Root draft PR: https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/pull/295

title: feat: add verified merch store reputation
body:
## Resultado

Integra de extremo a extremo la reputación comercial verificada con el dominio canónico de tiendas de artista del PR base #274: persistencia, elegibilidad, enlace seguro de comprador invitado, eventos operativos confiables, agregación versionada, API/OpenAPI, clientes generados, web, móvil, moderación, apelaciones, insignias, notificaciones opt-in, descubrimiento limitado, pruebas y runbook.

Este PR no despliega, no activa staging/producción, no habilita cobros, no importa ratings externos, no crea evaluaciones reales y no modifica datos reales. Los nueve flags permanecen apagados fuera de desarrollo.

Documentación: `docs/merch-reputation.md`, `docs/merch-reputation-acceptance.md` y `docs/runbooks/merch-reputation.md`. Companion móvil: https://github.com/diegueins680/TDF-mobile/pull/52, head exacto `da0c2f9188b75ab60e63050c9d58fe12181c7494`; [Mobile Validate 34450538338](https://github.com/diegueins680/TDF-mobile/actions/runs/34450538338) y [Datadog Synthetic 34450538337](https://github.com/diegueins680/TDF-mobile/actions/runs/34450538337), exitosos.

## Dependencia y modelo de dominio

- Base requerida: #274 (`feat/artist-merch-storefronts`), head exacto `05f45a6ef90eddb00b61053cd690e87c4cd061b5`; companion móvil basado en #49, `15c3cdb12503dfd07ad6b40a1cd7a9e40c45df55`. La extensión consume `merch_store`, membresías, productos, órdenes, líneas, checkout, fulfillment, shipments e incidencias canónicos mediante vistas adaptadoras; no crea copias.
- Fuentes durables: vínculo de comprador invitado, evaluación, revisión inmutable, dimensiones, media referenciada, respuesta/revisión, evidencia, señal operativa, source event, evento de reputación, reporte, caso, decisión, apelación, auditoría, política/caso de riesgo, insignia y notificación segura.
- Proyecciones reconstruibles: agregado de tienda, agregado de producto y dimensiones, siempre con `formula_version_id`.
- La reputación comunitaria/profesional existente no participa en tablas, fórmulas ni ranking comercial. El perfil público rotula “Reputación comercial”; cada tienda conserva su sujeto y nunca hereda score de propietarios, colaboradores, bandas u otras tiendas.
- La reseña preliminar `merch_review` del módulo base permanece separada; la evaluación completa vive en `merch_reputation_review`.

## Estados e invariantes

- Orden canónica `created|confirmed|cancelled|completed`; evaluación `published|hidden|limited|removed`; agregado `new_store|unrated|published`; confianza `new|limited|moderate|strong`; moderación `open|in_review|awaiting_evidence|provisionally_hidden|decided|appealed|closed`.
- Entrega o retiro confirmados habilitan 30 días. Cancelación sólo permite experiencia de tienda en comunicación/resolución; ninguna línea no recibida valora producto.
- Una evaluación de tienda por orden y una de producto por línea elegible, con índices únicos, locks y validación transaccional de autor, tienda, producto, línea, rango y ventana.
- Se bloquean propietario, administradores, colaboradores, artista titular y miembros verificables de la banda; no se usa fingerprinting.
- Ediciones requieren revisión esperada y conservan historial inmutable. Devolución, reembolso o disputa no borran evidencia. Fraude confirmado impide nueva elegibilidad y excluye proyecciones públicas hasta una corrección auditable.
- El valor de compra no forma parte de la evaluación ni de la fórmula. Una nota baja no abre riesgo ni produce sanción financiera, despublicación, bloqueo, cancelación o daño reputacional personal.

## Flujo de evidencia y agregación

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  O[Orden/checkout canónico] --> C[Claim privado: token hash + sesión]
  O --> F[Pago y fulfillment verificados]
  C --> E[Elegibilidad backend]
  F --> E
  E --> R[Evaluación + revisión inmutable]
  F --> Q[Outbox source_event transaccional]
  Q --> S[Señal sólo con evidencia y atribución suficientes]
  R --> X[Evento durable]
  S --> X
  X --> P[Proyector idempotente / checkpoint]
  P --> ST[Agregado tienda]
  P --> PR[Agregado producto]
  P --> B[Insignias]
  R --> M[Reporte / moderación]
  M --> A[Apelación independiente]
  M --> X
```

- El claim de checkout invitado valida SHA-256 de `lookup_token_hash`, bloquea la orden, no persiste ni registra el token, no reasigna comprador y responde 404 indistinguible ante orden/token/cuenta inválidos.
- Triggers capturan hechos saneados y sin PII desde fulfillment, shipment, cambios de orden e incidencias en la misma transacción.
- El worker usa `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, checkpoint y claves de fuente: un fallo conserva el evento para reintento; el replay no duplica señales.
- Sólo hay señal automática con promesa temporal/evidencia/atribución suficientes. Handoff puntual seguido de retraso courier no penaliza; despacho tardío del vendedor sí puede hacerlo.

## Fórmula v1 y sensibilidad

`merch-commercial-bayes-v1` vive en una fila versionada e inmutable:

- prior bayesiano 3.5, fuerza 5;
- vida media 730 días y periodo público principal 365 días;
- compradores 85 %, operación atribuible al vendedor máximo 15 %; sin evidencia operativa se usa sólo compradores;
- mínimo cinco órdenes evaluables y al menos una evaluación visible antes de publicar número;
- redondeo a un decimal; confianza limitada `<10`, moderada `10–29`, fuerte `>=30`; volumen histórico separado;
- contribución reputacional al ranking máximo 12 %, sólo tras `search_influence`.

Sensibilidad con ratings recientes homogéneos y sin operación: con 5 evaluaciones produce 2.3/3.3/4.3 para ratings 1/3/5; con 20 produce 1.5/3.1/4.7. La validación rechaza comprador `<80 %`, operación `>20 %`, vida media `<365`, umbral `<5` o ranking `>20 %`. Todo cambio exige otra versión y nuevas pruebas.

El listado canónico compone primero relevancia, disponibilidad, categoría y exploración/novedad; sólo entonces suma la contribución acotada. Tiendas sin score publicado o recién activadas reciben impulso base y etiqueta de descubrimiento, no una calificación artificial.

## Moderación, apelación y debido proceso

- Motivos: opinión negativa legítima, ofensivo, PII, spam, extorsión, conflicto, falsedad, coordinación, duplicación e irrelevancia.
- Flujo: triage, solicitud de evidencia, ocultamiento provisional reversible, restauración/limitación, decisión motivada y apelación.
- Cambia visibilidad; nunca borra revisiones ni evidencia originales.
- Apelación exige revisor distinto del apelante y decisor original.
- Riesgo objetivo exige política versionada, evidencia, permiso y auditoría. Consecuencia financiera importante exige revisión humana independiente; la política inicial queda `draft`.

## Permisos y threat model

| Amenaza | Control |
| --- | --- |
| Autoevaluación/cuentas relacionadas | sesión backend, ownership/membresía/banda verificable, sin fingerprinting |
| Enumeración/claim de orden | UUID + capacidad privada, hash server-side, 404 uniforme, token fuera de body/URL/log |
| Replay/concurrencia | idempotency key + request hash + locks + índices únicos + revisión esperada |
| Acceso cruzado vendedor | membresía activa y alcance de tienda en cada lectura/mutación |
| Score/operación inventados por cliente | sin endpoint de score; estados canónicos y proyección servidor |
| PII/XSS/media insegura | DTO cerrado, límites, storage key segura, MIME/tamaño/dimensiones/hash/scan/moderación/alt |
| Extorsión/brigading/Sybil | compra verificada, unicidad, reportes, moderación, métricas de crecimiento y relaciones internas |

Público nunca recibe orden, correo, dirección, teléfono, pago, tracking o despacho. Comprador, vendedor, moderador, riesgo y finanzas tienen acciones separadas y auditadas.

## UX web y móvil

- Perfil de artista, discovery, storefront, producto, carrito/checkout, seguimiento e historial muestran estados comerciales separados.
- Flujo poscompra nativo/web, preferencias, panel vendedor y moderación; producto, atención y logística no se mezclan.
- Respuesta del vendedor no modifica la evaluación; reporte y resultado quedan trazables.
- ES/EN en superficies nuevas, semántica accesible, teclado/foco, targets táctiles, reflow y texto ampliado. Comparación por tarjetas no es obligatoria y permanece detrás de flag.
- Video e incentivos quedan fuera del MVP.

## Migración y rollback

- `2026-09-08_merch_reputation.sql` es aditiva, reejecutable y corre después de `2026-09-07_artist_merch_storefronts.sql`; no fabrica ratings ni scores.
- Todas las tiendas empiezan `new_store`; sólo evidencia histórica inequívoca podría vincularse en un backfill futuro.
- El rollback sólo elimina una instalación prístina y no toca comercio canónico. Se niega ante claims, evaluaciones, fuentes, señales, auditoría, apelaciones, riesgo o notificaciones durables; en uso se apagan flags y se corrige hacia adelante.
- Catálogo de producción y verificaciones de release incluyen ambas migraciones con commits introductores inmutables.

## Pruebas y resultados

Validación local integrada sobre root `04d596ab2605e3747dfd00bc7aac28c3cf8675ce` y móvil `da0c2f9188b75ab60e63050c9d58fe12181c7494`:

- `stack test`: 2.501 ejemplos, 0 fallos.
- `./scripts/test-artist-merch-runtime.sh`: 1 ejemplo, 0 fallos, con HTTP autenticado y PostgreSQL sintético.
- `./scripts/test-merch-reputation-migration.sh`: pasó replay, concurrencia, constraints, fórmula, moderación/apelación, courier, reconstrucción y rollback seguro.
- `./scripts/test-artist-merch-storefronts-migration.sh`: pasó, incluidos reembolsos, disputas, liquidaciones, reejecución y rollback.
- `/bin/sh scripts/test-verified-experience-reviews-migration.sh`: pasó. El archivo no tiene bit ejecutable, por lo que esa es la invocación reproducible.
- Jest web focal: 5 suites, 20 pruebas, 0 fallos.
- Jest móvil completo: 68 suites, 327 pruebas, 0 fallos; la nueva pantalla poscompra añade 4 pruebas de estados, localización/DTO, reset de borrador y recuperación.
- `npm run release:check` móvil, lint web, build web de producción y presupuesto de bundle pasaron; bundle inicial 418.474 bytes gzip y sólo permanece el warning existente de chunk >500 KiB.
- OpenAPI y clientes web/móvil fueron regenerados después de integrar las bases y quedaron sin diff.
- `npm run quality:repo`, auditoría formal, contrato de release (59 pruebas) y catálogo estricto (1.052 candidatos, cero no revisados, obsoletos o IDs de decisión duplicados) pasaron.
- Build iOS release-simulator x86_64 pasó con API/credenciales sintéticas locales y OTA deshabilitado únicamente en el artefacto local. Maestro completó el flujo nativo desde la URI canónica de Expo, envió exactamente una evaluación de tienda y confirmó “Review submitted · Editing available”, manteniendo separada la línea de producto. Evidencia local no versionada: `/private/tmp/merch-reputation-verified-review-2026-09-10.png` (136.804 bytes).

Validación alojada del head exacto:

- [CI 34450538324](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/34450538324): 11/11 jobs exitosos, incluidos backend integral, runtime merch autenticado, preflight del esquema de producción, migraciones, contratos/clientes, UI, móvil, repositorio y persona E2E.
- [Catalog list authority 34450538319](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/34450538319): exitoso.
- [Mobile Validate 34450538338](https://github.com/diegueins680/TDF-mobile/actions/runs/34450538338): 68/68 suites y 327/327 pruebas; release checks y Expo Doctor 17/17 exitosos.
- [Mobile Datadog Synthetic 34450538337](https://github.com/diegueins680/TDF-mobile/actions/runs/34450538337): exitoso.
- Cloudflare Pages terminó exitoso. Vercel no ejecutó el preview por el límite de builds de la cuenta (`build-rate-limit`); es un bloqueo de cuota externo, no un fallo observado del código.
- Los workflows raíz Safe Install y Datadog no admiten dispatch manual para este PR apilado; sus equivalentes de instalación/calidad se ejecutaron localmente y el CI exacto regeneró/verificó los clientes.

No se ejecutaron E2E contra staging o servicios reales, pruebas en dispositivo físico ni una auditoría manual completa de WCAG 2.2 AA. La evidencia es sintética y no equivale a validación con usuarios, órdenes o tiendas reales. Las aprobaciones anteriores fueron descartadas al avanzar el head; se requiere revisión humana nueva y no hay hilos de revisión abiertos.

## Rollout, monitoreo y rollback operativo

Orden: sintético local → staging → prueba interna con comprador/vendedor/moderador separados → tiendas piloto → reviews visibles sin ranking → insignias → influencia limitada monitorizada → GA. Cada capacidad tiene kill switch independiente.

Métricas sin PII: tasa/tiempo de evaluación, distribución, ediciones tras resolución, reportes/abuso, SLA de moderación, apelaciones/reversiones, conversión, concentración, visibilidad nueva, insignias y anomalías por categoría/grupo. Alertas: manipulación/crecimiento, source/proyección fallida o divergente, y concentración.

## Gates pendientes antes del piloto

- Conectar el uploader real con storage firmado y antivirus/CDR.
- Ejecutar E2E en staging con identidades separadas y auditoría responsive/WCAG 2.2 AA asistida.
- Aprobar fórmula, insignias y umbrales con producto, riesgo, soporte y cumplimiento.
- Validar con legal/privacidad bases jurídicas, retención, exportación, borrado/seudonimización, consentimiento y evidencia.
- Conectar dashboards/alertas al stack operativo y demostrar criterios de salida.
- Reejecutar el preview de Vercel cuando se libere la cuota de builds; el estado actual apunta explícitamente a `build-rate-limit`, mientras Cloudflare y el CI exacto pasaron.
- Obtener una aprobación humana fresca para `04d596ab2605e3747dfd00bc7aac28c3cf8675ce`; las aprobaciones de heads anteriores quedaron correctamente descartadas.

Estos son gates explícitos: el PR no autoriza producción ni uso con compradores o tiendas reales.

# Onboarding personal-draft session boundary — 2026-09-08

## Outcome

Buyer contact and public-booking profile drafts now follow the authenticated session boundary in the current browser tab. An anonymous draft is preserved through the intended sign-in continuation, and a refresh for the same account keeps it available. The storage helper now maintains a session-scoped registry, so future personal-draft keys using the helper inherit the same cleanup behavior. title: Artist merch storefronts (closed pilot)
body:
# Draft PR: Artist merch storefronts

## Problema y objetivo

TDF podía exhibir perfiles y operar otros tipos de comercio, pero “las bandas pueden vender merch” no era todavía una capacidad real. Este PR introduce un dominio específico de merch físico integrado con perfiles, comunidad y checkout canónico, con rollout cerrado y honesto.

## Estado anterior

Existían perfiles/directorio/comunidad, marketplace de activos, checkouts Datafast/PayPal/manual y administración. No existían tienda, producto físico, variante/SKU, stock, storefront ni orden de merch; la documentación la trataba como futura.

## Arquitectura

- Entidades `merch_*` para vendedor, catálogo, imágenes, inventario, orden, fulfillment, vínculo de casos refund, issues, reviews, settlement, outbox, analítica y auditoría.
- Reutilización de `party`, `directory_profile`, permisos/PartySelector, `/assets/serve`, `commerce_checkout_*`, `commerce_refund*` y `commerce_dispute`.
- Tokens opacos hasheados para carrito/orden y snapshots inmutables.
- API Servant/OpenAPI y clientes TypeScript regenerados.
- UI web completa para comprador/vendedor/staff, incluida cancelación sin pagar, triage de incidencias, autorización dual de refund sin ejecución, monitoreo read-only de disputas, pedidos filtrables con totales/exportación sin PII y liquidación manual con evidencia privada; móvil para compra, seguimiento, soporte y operación esencial.
- Dependencia móvil revisable: [TDF-mobile#49](https://github.com/diegueins680/TDF-mobile/pull/49).

## UX

Storefront integrado al perfil y marketplace; mensajes explícitos para revisión, pago pendiente, proveedor no disponible, stock cambiado y permisos. El panel de pedidos permite filtrar fulfillment, resume solo importes autorizados y exporta CSV operativo sin PII ni fórmulas ejecutables. Diseño responsive, controles táctiles y semántica accesible. Español/inglés en superficies nuevas. El móvil deriva configuración compleja al panel web responsive.

## Datos y estados

Producto: `draft → pending_review → published/sold_out/paused/rejected/archived`. Pago, orden, reserva, fulfillment, shipment, refund, disputa y settlement permanecen separados. Refund usa el ledger canónico, asignaciones de línea y `requested → approved`; solo un adapter futuro podrá avanzar a ejecución. Disputas son evidencia canónica de solo lectura. Comisión general 1000 bps sobre producto después de descuento; override auditable, incluido 0%.

Incidencias: vendedor puede revisar/responder/resolver casos operativos; cancelación pagada, refund, disputa y fraude solo se escalan a staff. Cerrar el caso nunca muta por implicación pago, refund o settlement.

## Seguridad y privacidad

Autorización backend por store/acción; elegibilidad reclamada/verificada; locks/constraints contra sobreventa y doble refund; idempotencia exacta con fingerprint/asignaciones; `paid` solo por evidencia server-side; refund con caso staff y aprobador independiente; disputa sin mutaciones desde merch; archivos decodificados/reencodados y object keys generados; referencias HTTPS/durables; analítica sin PII; auditoría append-only; settlement con doble control, evidencia privada e identidad independiente del preparador; flags cerrados y kill switches separados.

## Migración

- Apply: `tdf-hq/sql/2026-09-07_artist_merch_storefronts.sql`
- Rollback: `tdf-hq/sql/2026-09-07_artist_merch_storefronts_rollback.sql`
- Rehearsal: `scripts/test-artist-merch-storefronts-migration.sh`

Rollback se niega si existe evidencia comercial. No hay conversión automática de assets; los tests usan datos sintéticos.

## Pruebas ejecutadas

- Migración PostgreSQL aislada: PASS, incluida reejecución, concurrencia, expiración, pago, comisión, dos refunds parciales canónicos/asignados/aprobados/confirmados, reverso acumulado exacto de comisión, disputa, ajuste de settlement y rollback.
- Runtime handlers + HTTP Servant + PostgreSQL 16 temporal: `./scripts/test-artist-merch-runtime.sh` PASS 1/1 y agregado a `backend-quality`. Además del recorrido previo, cubre refund con replay exacto/conflicto, aprobación independiente sin proveedor, cancelación pre-ejecución, acceso negativo y disputa read-only sin cambiar pago/settlement.
- Backend Haskell: PASS, 2.489/2.489 ejemplos sobre la integración final con `main`.
- Reglas focalizadas posteriores: PASS 9/9 coincidencias `merch`.
- Build web: PASS; presupuesto inicial JS PASS (416.059 bytes gzip).
- Web y móvil typecheck: PASS.
- Jest web admin merch + API + exportación CSV: PASS 15/15; incluye contrato idempotente, Axe sin impactos serios/críticos sobre settlement, refund sin ejecución y disputas read-only.
- Jest móvil deep links: PASS 2/2.
- Android nativo API 36.1: `app:assembleDebug` PASS (481 tareas), APK instalado y runtime verificado con API sintética local. Pasaron deep link público, catálogo, producto, aviso de piloto y bloqueo accesible de compra (`enabled=false`); sin excepciones TDF en logcat. Capturas reales obtenidas localmente.
- iOS nativo: Xcode 16.2 / iOS 18.3 Simulator / iPhone 16 `x86_64`. CocoaPods quedó sincronizado con las dependencias Expo declaradas; `pod install --deployment` y el build Release sin firma terminaron PASS. El `.app` se instaló y verificaron deep links de catálogo, storefront y producto contra fixture local read-only; el CTA de compra permaneció deshabilitado, solo se registraron GET y no hubo logs `error`/`fault` de TDF. Expo Updates se apagó solo en el artefacto de prueba para fijar el bundle local. Capturas reales versionadas en `docs/artist-merch/media/`. Dispositivo físico no ejecutado.
- Playwright Chromium desktop/Pixel 7: PASS 4/4, con capturas de runtime adjuntas al reporte.
- Axe en recorridos públicos: PASS, sin impactos serios/críticos.
- Regresión móvil global: 319/320 en una corrida simultánea; la única prueba con timeout pasó aislada 15/15.
- Regresión web global: la suite preexistente de administración de cursos falló durante la corrida simultánea; queda por repetir en CI/aislamiento. Las pruebas específicas de merch pasaron.
- OpenAPI YAML + regeneración web/móvil: PASS; clientes generados byte-idénticos (`aacf791d…`).
- Verificador del manifiesto de release: PASS 59/59 sobre el `main` final.
- Feature generation: PASS; auditoría conserva un fallo preexistente no relacionado en `/reputation/consents`.
- Auditoría de listas/catálogos: PASS, 1.011/1.011 candidatos clasificados; estados refund revisados como límites financieros cerrados y no como configuración editable.
- Gate remoto del PR: PASS 17/17 en la corrida que incluyó explícitamente el runtime HTTP autenticado dentro de `backend-quality`, además de migraciones, contratos, UI, móvil, E2E y auditoría de listas. El estado del HEAD vigente debe consultarse en GitHub; los previews automáticos no se consideran staging ni producción.

No se ejecutó dispositivo físico ni integración real con proveedor de pagos. La verificación iOS realizada corresponde exclusivamente a un Simulator local con API sintética; no equivale a TestFlight, staging o producción.

## Configuración y staging

Todos los flags permanecen `false`. Staging debe configurar de forma independiente storefront, solicitud, catálogo, checkout runtime, proveedor, reviews, notificaciones y experimentos. También debe proporcionar `MERCH_SETTLEMENT_EVIDENCE_DIR` como volumen privado, durable, cifrado y respaldado. Sin credenciales sandbox y evidencia de adapter, checkout debe continuar cerrado.

## Riesgos

- Los adapters específicos de pago/ejecución de refund e ingestión de disputas de merch todavía no están expuestos; el panel solo autoriza o lee evidencia.
- Falta validar workers/outbox y rate limiting en staging.
- Falta repetir en staging el E2E HTTP autenticado que ya pasó localmente y completar validación manual con lector/zoom.
- Definición fiscal, contractual y de protección al consumidor pendiente.

## Rollout y rollback

Local sintético → staging → prueba interna con dos adultos/roles → piloto cerrado → validación operativa/legal/contable → progresivo → GA. Rollback inicial por flags; migración destructiva solo antes de datos comerciales. Ver `docs/artist-merch/OPERATIONS.md`.

## Checklist bloqueante

- [ ] Adapters de pago/refund/dispute/reconcile verificados en sandbox.
- [x] Solicitud/asignación/idempotencia/aprobación dual/cancelación pre-ejecución de refund y disputa read-only verificadas con datos sintéticos.
- [x] E2E HTTP local de comprador invitado/vendedor/staff y cross-tenant con PostgreSQL 16 temporal.
- [ ] Repetición E2E en staging con observabilidad y personas/roles separados.
- [ ] Responsive/WCAG/teclado/lector/zoom con evidencia.
- [ ] Observabilidad y soporte on-call.
- [ ] Vendedor formal, facturación, impuestos/retenciones.
- [ ] Acuerdo vendedor, privacidad, consumidor, IP y productos prohibidos.
- [x] Flujo técnico local de evidencia final de settlement, doble control e idempotencia con datos sintéticos.
- [ ] Conciliación humana/contable del settlement ejercitada en staging con evidencia autorizada.

## Alcance diferido

Descargas digitales, multicurrency/países, cart multi-vendedor, couriers automáticos, payouts automáticos, chat nuevo y reviews públicas hasta cerrar moderación.
