title: fix: enforce event and reaction privacy boundaries
body:
## Problem

Locally authored events were exempt from the canonical visibility gate, so an authenticated non-owner could list or open events marked private or held in a non-public workflow state. Event-moment responses also enumerated every reactor Party identifier and timestamp even though clients need only total counts and caller-selected state.

## Changes

- allow event owners to retain access to drafts and private events
- require valid metadata that does not mark an event private plus the persisted public-listable workflow capability for every other ordinary Party
- keep strict administrator visibility and return a generic not-found response for hidden routes
- preserve one reaction response row per stored reaction while returning identity/time only for the caller row
- update the canonical OpenAPI contract and regenerate both web and mobile clients
- add backend and mobile regression coverage, including private list/detail/moment routes and anonymous count compatibility
- pin the separately published mobile commits from TDF-mobile draft PR 48

## Evidence

Local:
- backend affected group: 20 examples, 0 failures
- backend full Hspec: 2476 examples, 0 failures
- web Jest: 185 suites, 1757 tests passed
- web typecheck and production build: passed; bundle budget 5 preloads / 412191 gzip bytes
- web lint: 0 errors, 102 existing warnings
- mobile Jest: 67 suites, 369 tests passed
- mobile typecheck and lint: passed
- catalog audit: passed
- CI pipeline tests: 16 passed
- production release tests: 49 passed
- required mobile OpenAPI generation: passed; generated client hashes match
- diff checks: passed

Hosted at head 57004ccacc02d083cd030ff3d797897a537daad4:
- 15 checks passed
- 1 expected migration scope check skipped
- 0 failed or pending
- backend-quality passed in 35m04s and aggregate quality passed
- Vercel and Cloudflare feature previews completed; they are not production validation

Detailed report: reports/event-moment-privacy-audit-2026-09-08.md

## Risks and compatibility

The response remains count-compatible but non-caller reactors now have null identity/time. Consumers that improperly depended on enumerating other Party IDs must adapt. Events without valid non-private metadata and a public-listable lifecycle state now fail closed for non-owners; owners and strict administrators retain access. No database migration or dependency change is included.

## Rollback

Revert the root commits and matching mobile commits together. No stored data transformation is required.

## Remaining gaps

No staging/PostgreSQL route request, production validation, native device session, screen-reader session, new screenshot, or field-performance measurement was performed. Concurrent different-type reaction exclusivity and comment/author privacy remain deferred. This PR is stacked on the prior first-action evidence PR.

title: Onboarding: require durable reaction and artist evidence
body:
## Problem

`moment_reaction` onboarding completion trusted a client claim, and retrying the toggle after a lost response could remove a successfully stored reaction. The real mobile artist-follow action wrote `ArtistFollow`, while completion checked the unrelated `FanFollow` domain; person-to-person follows were also mislabeled as artist activation. Mobile local moment content shared a device-global store across accounts.

## Changes

- Require Party-bound, in-window `event_moment/reaction_added` evidence before completing `moment_reaction`.
- Accept optional `emrrActive` desired state while preserving legacy toggle behavior when omitted.
- Write reaction activation and append-only evidence in one transaction; retain historical evidence after removal and avoid duplicate evidence on retry.
- Write real artist-follow evidence atomically and make `artist_followed` completion read that shared evidence vocabulary.
- Advance the mobile submodule to a published commit that verifies returned remote state, binds auth sessions, removes false person-follow analytics, scopes local moments by Party, and surfaces storage failures.
- Update canonical OpenAPI, regenerate both clients, and add backend/mobile regression coverage.

## Evidence

- Freshly linked full Hspec: 2,474 examples, 0 failures.
- Focused moment Hspec: 2 examples, 0 failures.
- Focused artist-follow Hspec: 1 example, 0 failures.
- Mobile: 67 suites / 368 tests passed; typecheck and strict lint passed.

title: feat(onboarding): make saved events authoritative across devices
body:
## Problem

The onboarding path treated “save an event” as client/device state rather than a durable, authenticated first useful action. That prevented reliable cross-device continuity and allowed client assertions to complete onboarding without server evidence.

During revalidation, the audit also reproduced a critical anonymous-data boundary defect: the public event projection did not enforce `metadata.isPublic`, so an explicitly private event could enter public event, venue, and search projections when its workflow status was otherwise listable.

## Implemented

- Adds an additive, idempotent PostgreSQL migration that repairs public event projection with a fail-closed privacy predicate and removes only stale derived search documents.
- Adds canonical favorite identifiers and public-eligibility checks for event, venue, profile, and classified targets.
- Makes new favorite creation and append-only `favorite.saved` evidence atomic; duplicate saves remain idempotent and create no duplicate completion evidence.
- Requires Party-bound, in-window server evidence before `event_saved` can complete onboarding.
- Makes web saved-event state server-authoritative with explicit loading/error/ready states, desired-state writes, accessible control state, and sign-in intent continuity.
- Updates the mobile gitlink to [TDF-mobile draft PR #46](https://github.com/diegueins680/TDF-mobile/pull/46), which adds Party-scoped server authority, connectivity-only fallback, account-switch cancellation, and truthful completion timing.
- Updates OpenAPI, regenerated web/mobile clients, contract tests, component/backend tests, migration verification, and the consolidated audit report.

## Evidence and tests

- Backend executable build: passed.
- Full Hspec: 2,472 examples, 0 failures.
- Focused Hspec: canonicalization 37 examples / 0 failures; event-save 1 example / 0 failures.
- Disposable PostgreSQL 16 migration test: passed, including old-defect reproduction, two migration applications, privacy cases, stale-search repair, legacy convergence, atomic save/audit/idempotence/delete.
- Required mobile generation with `REQUIRE_MOBILE_WORKSPACE=1`: passed; web/mobile generated SHA-1 matched (`1c9284bb97dd954525840f304216582d92abae77`).
- Directory contract test: passed.
- Production release tests: 50/50 passed.
- Catalog-list deterministic test: 1/1 passed.
- Exact catalog-list authority audit: passed with zero unreviewed candidates and zero stale decisions after carrying forward the reviewed migration/mobile-registry fingerprints and classifying the test-only DTO fixture.
- Web focused Jest: 2 suites / 5 tests passed.
- Web full Jest: 185 suites / 1,757 tests passed.
- Web typecheck/build: passed; build retains the existing large-chunk warning.
- Web lint: 0 errors, 102 pre-existing warnings; changed-file lint clean.
- Mobile full Jest: 66 suites / 349 tests passed; TypeScript and ESLint (`--max-warnings=0`) passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Required doctor: 14 ok, 4 warnings, 0 errors; warnings are documented in the report.

No staging/production migration, real transaction, real communication, browser screenshot, native device run, screen-reader run, field analytics validation, merge, or deployment occurred.

The first root CI run exposed the catalog-list fingerprint drift (3 unreviewed, 2 stale). It was reproduced locally, attributed to the registered migration, the current generated mobile registry, and one test response fixture, repaired without changing business authority, and the formerly failing `hardcoded-list-audit` passed on the current GitHub head.

## Migration and rollout risk

The new application behavior depends on the production migration being reviewed and applied through the authorized release process. The migration is additive and tested twice on a disposable database. It intentionally has no confidentiality-weakening rollback: restoring the old view could re-expose private events, so recovery should be a forward repair or stricter replacement.

Deploy ordering should place the database migration before clients depend on the new favorite function/evidence semantics. Mobile publication remains separately gated by PR #46 and manual EAS release controls.

## Rollback

- Revert application/client commits if required, while preserving the stricter public-event view.
- Do not restore the former projection definition.
- Correct database issues with a reviewed forward migration.
- Revert the parent mobile gitlink if the mobile PR is not accepted; do not reference an unpublished submodule commit.

## Dependencies and remaining gaps

This is a stacked draft based on onboarding draft PR #241 (`feature/onboarding-continuity-20260906`) so its diff stays focused. Retarget to `main` after #241 merges.

Deferred: authorized staging/production migration verification, real two-device/account tests, native accessibility/runtime checks, ES/EN catalog migration for the touched mobile journey, batched saved-event detail hydration, field Core Web Vitals/funnel baselines, durable evidence for `moment_reaction`, and the paused experiment measurement contract.

Full findings, capability matrix, coverage, exact commands/results, historical revalidation, risks, and usability script: `reports/event-save-continuity-audit-2026-09-07.md`.

title: Make event saves account authoritative
body:
# Event-save account continuity

Execution date: 2026-09-07 (America/Guayaquil)

Root branch: `feature/event-save-continuity-20260907`

Mobile branch: `feature/event-save-continuity-20260907`

## Outcome

Saved events now converge through the existing Party-owned `directory_favorite` capability instead of remaining device-only. The protected favorite API supports a validated `targetKind` filter, accepts event saves only for positive IDs in the public event projection, and omits previously saved events that are no longer public from event-filtered reads. PUT and DELETE retain idempotent desired-state behavior.

Mobile keeps a Party-scoped cache and a Party-scoped last-desired-state outbox. Reads reconcile against `GET /directory/favorites?targetKind=event`; online writes wait for server acknowledgment, while retryable network/server failures leave a durable local operation for replay. Operations for one Party are serialized, rapid toggles reconcile first, and successful replay retries the onboarding completion handshake. Non-retryable API failures do not remain in the outbox or produce completion analytics.

The unscoped legacy key remains unread during normal saved-event access. The profile saved tab exposes only a count and a confirmation explaining that ownership is unknown. Values are bound to the current Party only after that explicit action; transfer to the Party-scoped cache/outbox completes before the legacy key is removed.

`event_saved` onboarding completion now requires a Party-owned favorite created between authoritative signup and the completion request and joined to the current public event projection. Missing, cross-Party, pre-signup, future, and non-public evidence fail closed; valid evidence completes once.

## Verification

- Backend test target compiled and linked with GHC 9.10.3.
- Focused Hspec `--match event-save`: 1 example passed, covering missing, cross-Party, pre-signup, future, non-public, valid, and repeated completion cases.
- Mobile focused Jest: 2 suites, 13 tests passed.
- Mobile full Jest: 66 suites, 344 tests passed after the replay-completion assertion was added. The run emitted existing asynchronous `act()` warnings in `UserSettingsProvider`; no suite failed.
- Mobile TypeScript and ESLint passed with zero errors/warnings after the final sync changes.
- Web and mobile OpenAPI clients regenerated byte-for-byte equal.
- Web TypeScript passed against the regenerated contract.
- Strict catalog-list audit passed with no unreviewed or stale decision.
- Production-release safeguards passed 50/50; CI-scope safeguards passed 16/16.

## Scope and residual risk

No production data, migration, merge, deployment, experiment activation, or customer communication is part of this change. The existing table already has the required Party/kind/target primary key, so no schema migration is needed.

Tests use in-memory SQLite and mocked AsyncStorage/API calls. A real two-device session, app upgrade, iOS/Android storage interruption, accessibility pass, staging authentication, and production PostgreSQL query-plan/runtime check remain unperformed. Saved-event detail hydration still uses existing per-event requests after the synchronized ID read; batching that payload is a separate performance improvement.

The onboarding experiment remains paused because `moment_reaction` evidence and assignment/exposure semantics are still not fully server-authoritative.

## Summary

- add a durable test/staging reputation aggregation outbox and worker with fenced leases, retries, recoverable DLQ cycles, immutable audit evidence, bounded run results, deterministic candidate calculation, and non-identifying health metrics
- aggregate ordinal ranks as Bayesian Bradley--Terry pairwise wins/losses/ties, blend comparable absolute scores through a neutral anchor, refresh each connected comparison component atomically, and enforce evaluator caps against the exact adjusted effective total
- freeze activated formulas and run high-water marks; keep bounded-run output separate from live candidates; fail bounded runs closed across post-cutoff evaluation, interaction, rank, role, and category mutations
- serialize run creation with source transactions through an exclusive/shared transaction fence, use commit-ordered automatic-event timestamps, preserve event-ID idempotency, and retain a bounded coverage watermark whenever automatic evidence is intentionally suppressed
- serialize run completion with run-backed enqueue operations, reject terminal-run work, and permit success only after every event belonging to the run is processed
- invalidate both old and new tuples when evaluations, interactions, or ranks move; fan category changes across both pre-change and post-change eligible scopes; fan role changes across affected comparison peers only from submitted, eligible, observable, processable evidence while retaining former-role removal coverage
- support irreversible planned-to-cancelled and running-to-terminal lifecycles, while claiming run-backed events only for running runs in the requested environment
- schedule stale simulation candidates for active/draft formulas once per UTC day, dead-letter expired final-attempt leases before incrementing, and keep `reputation_public_aggregate` untouched
- add defense-in-depth production gates in process configuration, release configuration, and the database control plane; register the migration and document the staging runbook, observability, rollback, and governance status

## Safety boundaries

- disabled by default
- worker rejects enabled production mode
- database constraints prevent enabling the production control row
- automatic producers remain suppressed when no simulation consumer or open bounded run exists, and advance a coverage watermark so later historical runs cannot cross unrecorded evidence
- only test/staging claims are accepted and only simulation-mode candidates or immutable bounded-run results are written
- this PR does not deploy, run production migrations, enable any flag, or start a pilot

- add Party-bound signup, intent, eligibility, completion, and first-value persistence
- expose authenticated onboarding APIs and regenerate web/mobile contracts
- switch web and mobile completion analytics to the atomic `newlyCompleted` result
- require Party-bound, in-window server evidence before accepting `artist_followed` or `access_requested` completion
- resume artist-follow, directory contact, and supported product intent safely after authentication
- retain mobile intent for retry after transient sync failure and expose the supported internships path
- isolate mobile saved events by authenticated Party, preserve ambiguous legacy/corrupt data, and surface storage failures without false success analytics
- add production migration guards, a disposable PostgreSQL rehearsal, and a consolidated continuity audit

The parent onboarding PRs have merged, so this root draft and mobile draft PR #40 now target `main` directly.

## Verification

- catalog list audit: passed
- production-release tests: 49/49 passed
- CI-pipeline tests: 16/16 passed
- onboarding migration forward/idempotency/constraints/cascade/non-destructive rollback/reapply: passed on disposable PostgreSQL 16
- focused web Jest: 5 suites, 27 tests passed on the second-batch tree
- web TypeScript and scoped changed-file lint: passed
- web production build and initial-bundle check: passed; 12,415 modules, 5 preloads / 412,162 gzip bytes, with Vite's existing large-chunk warning
- web lint: 0 errors and 102 existing warnings; direct full-source `eslint --quiet` passed
- the current 184-module backend test target compiled and linked; another process then reacquired Stack's lock before test launch, so the blocked wrapper was stopped and the freshly linked executable passed onboarding 3/3 plus access-request evidence 1/1, including missing, cross-Party, pre-signup, future, valid, and repeated-claim cases
- mobile focused saved-event/component Jest: 2 suites, 9 tests passed
- mobile final full Jest after saved-event containment: 66 suites, 340 tests passed with `REQUIRE_MOBILE_WORKSPACE=1`; typecheck and full lint passed
- regenerated web/mobile API clients match byte-for-byte

The artist-follow and access-request evidence SQLite cases compiled and passed locally via the freshly linked test executable. The interrupted Stack wrapper is not counted as a passing command; hosted CI status is reported against the published PR head at handoff.

A full web Jest attempt before this continuation's final reconciliation reproduced the unrelated `CourseRegistrationsAdminPage` timeout/overlapping-`act()` cascade from the stacked baseline and an unrelated `PromoCodeField` failure. The run was stopped after those failures; the touched onboarding suites were rerun separately and passed 12/12. No test was disabled or weakened.

## Risks and rollback

- artist-follow and access-request completion are now server-evidence-backed; event saves and reactions remain client-observed, so the paused experiment must remain paused until every included action and account-bound exposure semantics are authoritative
- mobile saved events remain device-local even though onboarding completion is now account-durable; their on-device cache is Party-scoped, corrupt data is preserved, the unowned legacy key is quarantined, and remote convergence/import remain deferred
- directory contact has safe routing/helper/build coverage but no authenticated browser-component run
- no new browser, native-device, real OAuth, staging email, payment, production database, or representative analytics validation was performed in this batch
- application rollback is non-destructive: the additive onboarding table and its account history remain in place; no destructive down migration is included

No merge or deployment is requested by this draft. No production data, real transaction, customer communication, or experiment activation occurred.

## Evidence

See `reports/onboarding-continuity-audit-2026-09-06.md` for the capability matrix, coverage matrix, finding IDs, implementation inventory, exact limitations, and next-batch acceptance criteria.

title: Onboarding-first account entry, privacy, and mobile continuity
body:
# Onboarding-first account entry, privacy, and mobile continuity

## Problem

TDF onboarding and first-purchase journeys contained security/privacy risks and task dead ends: self-signup passed a chosen password into a welcome-email/log path; PostHog could receive reset-token URLs and personal identity properties; recovery transport failures appeared successful; general signup asked for unrelated optional choices; two acquisition links lost/doubled intent; mobile could retain a revoked session and trap anonymous ticket buyers behind a spinner; no-quote booking success sent customers toward a staff calendar; and an empty marketplace promised notifications without sending a request.

## Changes

- Remove chosen passwords, reset tokens, names, and emails from unconfigured email fallbacks; introduce credential-free self-signup confirmation content.
- Sanitize direct and nested sensitive analytics properties and URL query values, disable DOM autocapture, enable personal-data masking, identify only with opaque party ID, and preserve only PostHog's SDK-injected configured project token required for ingestion.
- Simplify signup to immediate fields, semantic forms, autocomplete, Enter submission, server-matching password policy, truthful recovery, bounded auth requests, safe intent continuity, and theme-readable helper text.
- Correct TDF general CTA and distribution return parameter.
- Clear mobile auth state on authoritative null session, use authenticated Party identity instead of settings fallbacks, and preserve event context for anonymous native ticket buyers through authentication.
- Keep quote-backed booking orders on secure public tracking while removing the staff-only destination from no-quote confirmations.
- Remove unsupported marketplace notification capture; keep new booking/marketplace contact drafts in current-tab storage and discard legacy persistent PII instead of restoring it on shared browsers.
- Reject malformed public review payloads at the API boundary so the existing recoverable error state renders instead of dereferencing invalid data.
- Programmatically label repeated Domo campaign controls and correct the static audit's `inputProps` recognition.
- Add focused unit/browser/mobile tests, real before/after screenshots, lab performance evidence, and the consolidated audit.

## Evidence

- Exact reviewed root head: `7876ed55fa140ef09466a5281e3c40123b6f04e9`.
- Audit: `reports/onboarding-first-ux-audit-2026-09-05.md`
- Screenshots/performance: `artifacts/ux-audit-2026-09-05/`
- Combined privacy/analytics regression: 5 suites / 32 tests passed. The current focused analytics regression also passed 5/5, including retention of the required PostHog project token while application and nested token fields remain stripped.
- Exact integrated web Jest run: 182/183 suites and 1,577/1,745 tests passed; the one unchanged 24k-line course-registration suite hit a 5-second test timeout and cascaded 168 later failures. Its immediate isolated rerun passed 526/526 tests, and every PR-touched suite passed in the full run.
- Full current public-persona browser regression: 16 passed / 2 intentional duplicate-device skips; focused commerce evidence also passed 4/4 on desktop and Pixel 7 with axe serious/critical checks and screenshots.
- Exact integrated web typecheck and production build passed; bundle guard reports 5 preloads / 411,815 gzip bytes initial JS.
- Full lint passed with 0 errors and the existing 102-warning baseline; targeted lint for both review fixes passed. Static UI audit reports zero findings; automation tests passed 42/42.
- Static-audit parser regressions: 5/5 passed; current UI source has zero static findings.
- Mobile full Jest: 64 suites / 318 tests passed; typecheck, lint, Mobile Validate, Datadog, and local Expo/Metro startup passed at `394479d708c92ca6470bd8a2e9551ea03bab7aec`.
- Backend/application and the 184-module test executable compiled/linked; the matched credential-content Hspec test ran 1 example with 0 failures. Existing compiler warnings remain visible; SMTP delivery is not claimed.
- Codex review findings for light-theme helper-text contrast and PostHog ingestion metadata were fixed and resolved; the fresh review on the exact root head found no further major issues.
- Lab LCP remains about 4.3 seconds in both variants; no performance uplift is claimed.

## Risks and migrations

- No database migration, new dependency, price/policy change, role assignment change, or production action.
- General signup no longer asks for optional marketing choice or unrelated favorite artists; backend payload remains compatible (`marketingOptIn:false`).
- Analytics is intentionally less identifying; dashboards depending on username/display name/roles or DOM autocapture must use privacy-safe aggregate dimensions instead.
- Parent mobile pointer references the exact audited PR #39 head, now merged into mobile `main` as `9ff71507730808b4a52e8fa6e25d1ca366783543` after independent approval.
- Mobile review and merge evidence is tracked in [TDF-mobile PR #39](https://github.com/diegueins680/TDF-mobile/pull/39).

## Rollback

Revert the focused root commits and reset the parent submodule pointer to the prior published mobile commit. Do not restore credential-bearing email/logging or token-bearing analytics behavior; if UI rollback is necessary, retain the security/privacy commit.

## Remaining gaps

- Durable account-bound onboarding completion and action resumption.
- Mixed-language legal/auth content and account-bound onboarding/action resumption.
- Mobile query/deep-link normalization and physical-device accessibility checks.
- OpenAPI/client drift, current-tab contact ownership across account changes, and authenticated campaign screen-reader/keyboard validation.
- Controlled field Web Vitals, real provider delivery/payment/OAuth, and staging validation.

All hosted checks are green on the exact root head, the required collaborator approval is current, and dependent mobile PR #39 is merged. No root merge or production deployment has been performed.

title: feat: migrate remaining web Party selectors
body:
## Resumen ejecutivo

Completa la migración de relaciones basadas en Party a selectores humanos reutilizables en backend, web y mobile. El usuario busca por nombre o `@username`; únicamente el `partyId` canónico seleccionado se transmite y persiste. La búsqueda es server-side, paginada, acotada, cancelable y autorizada por contexto funcional.

## Problema resuelto y alcance

- elimina campos y fallbacks visibles que exigían interpretar, copiar o escribir Party IDs;
- migra reservas, logística, feedback, operaciones, artistas, eventos, sesiones, pagos, chat, amistades y campañas;
- elimina descargas de `GET /parties` usadas para resolver relaciones en cliente;
- incorpora selección simple y múltiple con avatar/fallback, nombre, username y metadato secundario;
- completa la variante mobile, la privacidad de momentos/vCard y la resolución de relaciones sociales;
- deja una matriz de trazabilidad y una allowlist cerrada de las cuatro referencias técnicas administrativas justificadas.

## Arquitectura y decisiones

- `GET /parties/search` devuelve `PartySelectorPage`/`PartySelectorOption`, no `PartyDTO` completo.
- `PartySelector`, `UserSelector` y `PartyMultiSelector` comparten búsqueda, caché, cursor y semántica; mobile usa controles nativos y no replica la UI web.
- mínimo 2 caracteres alfanuméricos, debounce 300 ms, 15 resultados iniciales, máximo 20, cursor opaco acotado, carga incremental y hasta 100 exclusiones.
- React Query propaga `AbortSignal`, deduplica solicitudes y separa caché por identidad, roles, módulos, contexto, scope, filtros y consulta.
- las opciones elegidas permanecen en caché visual durante errores; texto libre nunca constituye una selección.
- cada instancia declara su contexto y filtros. `event_logistics` exige el evento mediante `scopeId`; `booking_engineer` exige el rol canónico activo de Engineer; pagos admite personas u organizaciones.
- el dominio aún no ofrece tenant/visibilidad/bloqueo canónicos para todas las Parties. No se inventaron filtros de cliente: esa limitación queda explícita y los contextos sociales se reducen en servidor a cuentas personales activas, excluyen al actor y aplican cuota.

## Base de datos y API

- OpenAPI añade `context`, `scopeId`, cursor documentado y respuesta `429`; clientes web/mobile se regeneraron desde la fuente canónica.
- ranking: username exacto, nombre exacto, prefijos, términos completos/parciales y una edición acotada.
- comparación insensible a mayúsculas, `@`, diacríticos y puntuación separadora; preserva la grafía original y soporta términos reordenados, apóstrofes, guiones y Unicode.
- el prefiltrado SQL y sus índices usan la misma forma compacta normalizada, por lo que `oneil` descubre `O'Neil` antes del ranking.
- credenciales, Parties, roles y avatares se resuelven por lotes, sin N+1; si existen varias credenciales se prioriza una activa de forma determinista.
- migración aditiva `2026-09-04_party_selector_trigram_indexes` conserva los índices generales existentes; `2026-09-04_party_selector_punctuation_indexes` añade seis índices compactos B-tree/GIN cuando `pg_trgm` está disponible. Ambas están en el manifest inmutable y tienen rollback independiente.
- no cambia ninguna FK ni formato de relación: nombres, usernames y avatares siguen siendo presentación dinámica.

## Seguridad y privacidad

- la autorización contextual se ejecuta en backend: CRM, Scheduling, Invoicing, Catalog, Ops o Internships según el flujo.
- `event_logistics` sólo permite buscar dentro de un evento concreto al organizador o a un editor; un viewer u otro usuario recibe denegación.
- `booking_engineer` limita resultados a Parties con asignación activa del rol canónico Engineer; el endpoint de escritura mantiene su validación final.
- `event_invitation` y `social_connection` exigen autenticación, fuerzan `person + active account`, excluyen al actor, omiten nombre legal y consumen 300 búsquedas/día por hash de Party.
- el DTO no contiene correo, teléfono, tax ID, notas ni contactos de emergencia; tampoco se almacenan términos en la cuota/telemetría.
- campañas dejaron de filtrar teléfono/correo en navegador; la elegibilidad final continúa validándose en su endpoint de escritura.
- la regla arquitectónica impide reintroducir IDs visibles fuera de `AdminTokenPage`, `AdminUsersPage`, `CourseRegistrationsAdminPage` y `LabelTracksPage`.
- web y mobile emiten métricas agregables de latencia, vacío, timeout/error, cancelación, avatar y selección sin consulta, Party ID, nombre, username, URL ni mensajes del servidor.

## Web y mobile

- web: combobox MUI con teclado, foco, ARIA live, retry, estados vacío/carga/error, paginación y chips removibles/deduplicados.
- mobile: selector nativo simple y múltiple, cursor/retry/cancelación, anuncios accesibles, chip removible y fallback si la imagen falta o falla.
- la identidad propia se deriva de sesión; momentos, vCard, chat y relaciones usan copias humanas y mantienen IDs sólo en payloads internos.

## Rendimiento

Pruebas reproducibles en PostgreSQL 16:

- el benchmark previo de 50.000 Parties/credenciales redujo nombre de 58,1 ms a 7,6 ms y username de 17,7 ms a 2,3 ms mediante bitmap GIN;
- la migración compacta fue aplicada y revertida en un clúster PG16 desechable; `EXPLAIN` mostró `Bitmap Index Scan on party_selector_display_name_compact_trgm_idx` y la consulta `%one%` devolvió `Anne-Marie O'Neil`;
- el rollback retiró los seis índices compactos y la re-aplicación queda protegida por `IF NOT EXISTS`;
- el orden SQL exacto-estable garantiza que una coincidencia exacta no quede fuera del lote candidato.

Esto valida el plan local, no sustituye el gate p95 de staging (<500 ms). La consulta permanece acotada a 401 candidatos por fuente y 20 respuestas.

## Matriz de flujos migrados

La auditoría completa con aplicación, archivo, flujo, comportamiento anterior, riesgo, solución, prueba y estado está en [`docs/party-selector.md`](docs/party-selector.md).

## Validación local

- backend completo: **2.464 ejemplos / 0 fallos** (`stack test`);
- web completo: **181 suites / 1.732 tests**;
- mobile completo: **64 suites / 314 tests**;
- typecheck web y mobile: pasa;
- ESLint mobile: pasa sin warnings; ESLint web: 0 errores y 102 warnings preexistentes del repositorio;
- build web de producción: pasa; presupuesto inicial **411.268 bytes gzip**;
- generación OpenAPI web/mobile repetida sin drift;
- PostgreSQL 16: apply, uso del índice compacto, coincidencia `oneil`/`O'Neil` y rollback verificados;
- release/migraciones: **44/44** pruebas del manifest pasan;
- auditoría de catálogos: pasa sin candidatos sin revisar ni decisiones obsoletas;
- `git diff --check`: pasa.

Todos los checks alojados sobre `c8e741d33` están verdes: backend, UI, mobile, E2E, contratos, migraciones, auditorías, builds y previews. El PR permanece draft para revisión humana.

## Despliegue

1. Aplicar el manifest revisado mediante el runner de producción; las dos migraciones son aditivas.
2. Publicar backend/OpenAPI.
3. Publicar web y luego mobile; los endpoints de escritura mantienen el mismo Party ID canónico.
4. Verificar p95, errores, timeouts y búsquedas vacías agregadas sin registrar términos.

No requiere downtime ni backfill de relaciones.

## Rollback

1. Revertir consumidores web/mobile y backend.
2. Ejecutar `2026-09-04_party_selector_punctuation_indexes_rollback.sql` y luego `2026-09-04_party_selector_trigram_indexes_rollback.sql` si se desea retirar los índices.
3. Conservar las relaciones existentes: ningún ID ni dato histórico se transforma.

## Evidencia visual

Los previews automáticos de Vercel y Cloudflare del head permiten revisar los flujos web responsive. La evidencia y validación nativa están enlazadas desde el draft PR mobile.

## Riesgos, limitaciones y pasos manuales

- medir p95 con cardinalidad/red de staging y capturar pantallas autenticadas requiere ese entorno; no se inventa una métrica de producción desde datos locales;
- tenant, bloqueo y visibilidad global requieren primero un modelo canónico de dominio; los contextos públicos aplican el cierre seguro disponible hoy;
- los cambios locales de memoria no relacionados están excluidos de todos los commits.

title: feat: contextual reputation foundation
body:
## Resumen

Introduce una base segura y auditable para evolucionar las reseñas verificadas a reputación contextual, sin convertir datos históricos en rankings inventados.

## Decisiones

- Separa físicamente evidencia verificable, evaluaciones, rankings privados y agregados públicos.
- Usa ROC para preferencias personales y prior bayesiano para reputación pública; las preferencias no afectan el puntaje público.
- Conserva reseñas actuales y exige feature flag/piloto antes de habilitar lectores o writers.

## Cambios

- Migración PostgreSQL aditiva e idempotente con rollback.
- Categorías institucionales traducidas, fórmula versionada y auditoría.
- Primitivas Haskell deterministas y pruebas para pesos, confianza y regularización.
- Prototipo web accesible: drag progresivo, teclado/touch alternativo, avatar de iniciales, exclusión, borrador y deshacer.
- Documentación de auditoría, UX, amenazas, privacidad, migración, rollback y pendientes externos.

## Pruebas

- `stack test --fast` quedó en espera del build-lock ocupado por compilaciones preexistentes; no se interrumpieron procesos ajenos.

## Riesgos y despliegue

No aplicar ni activar automáticamente. Seguir staging -> piloto consentido -> expansión gradual con los criterios de pausa/rollback documentados en `docs/contextual-reputation/README.md`.

## Pendientes externos

Legal/consentimiento, RBAC administrativo, infraestructura de worker/cola, contratos endpoint completos y validación E2E en dispositivos antes de activar.

title: fix: preserve applied production migration integrity
body:
## Summary

- restore three already-applied SQL migrations byte-for-byte to their production ledger checksums
- preserve the later commerce and distribution trigger fixes in two new idempotent forward migrations with explicit rollback files
- verify corrected function bodies during release and lock the historical checksums with regression tests
- update every affected migration harness and the reviewed technical-registry decision

## Rationale

The guarded production release for the studio internship audit stopped before any mutation because three historical migration files no longer matched the production ledger. Production remained on the prior image with 59 migrations, no audit table, and no advisory lock. This change repairs the repository without editing the production ledger or discarding the later functional corrections.

## Migration and rollback

Pending forward migrations:
- 2026-08-25_commerce_trigger_row_binding_compatibility
- 2026-08-25_distribution_trigger_row_binding_compatibility

Both are transactional, rerunnable CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION migrations. Their rollback files restore the historical function definitions. Freeze the corresponding checkout or distribution writes and roll back the application before applying those rollback files. The restored music-directory migration already has its registered forward host-compatibility migration. Never update applied ledger checksums manually.

## Verification

- npm run test:production-release: 45 passed
- npm run test:ci-pipeline: 16 passed
- npm run quality:repo: passed
- npm run audit:catalog-lists: passed with the pinned mobile submodule initialized
- local PostgreSQL 16 disposable rehearsal: all 67 migrations applied, schema verification passed, seven corrected functions verified, second execution was idempotent
- focused checkout behavior: invalid amount and environment rejected; valid payment and provider binding accepted
- git diff --check and shell syntax checks passed

Docker-specific migration scripts were not reported as locally successful because Docker Desktop was unresponsive. The equivalent SQL lifecycle was exercised on isolated local PostgreSQL; GitHub migration CI must still pass before merge.

## Security and operations

- no production secrets or customer data are committed
- no production ledger rows are changed
- no backend rollout, internship activation, assignment, external notification, payment, or provider action is performed by this PR
- production event discovery remains disabled during the future guarded rollout
- take a fresh database snapshot and run the exact-SHA release preflight before deployment

## Studio internship draft

This PR only unblocks the already-reviewed studio audit implementation in PR #200. The production project/task must remain an inactive, hidden, non-notifying draft associated with Stewart Moreira only after the backend is safely deployed and an authorized Manager/Admin session is supplied. Activation and notification remain separate approval gates.

body:
## Summary

Adds an explicit draft/activation lifecycle for the studio-management internship audit, normalized test plans/cases/executions and calculated completion controls, and an authenticated private reporting/triage workflow that extends the existing feedback system while preserving public feedback compatibility.

## Included

- Evidence-backed studio feature inventory and 174 deterministic Spanish test cases.
- Two-week Spanish Stewart guide, principal assignment content, daily/final summary model, and inactive draft preview.
- Reversible PostgreSQL migration and legacy feedback compatibility.
- Backend authorization for assigned intern, other intern, and authorized admin/manager behavior.
- Internal report drafts, structured context, multiple evidence, comments, information requests, duplicates, retests, audit history, search/filter/export, and GitHub linkage field.
- Responsive intern test-plan/report surfaces and administrator dashboard.
- In-app notifications, durable test-safe notification outbox, documented rules, and an explicit production-dispatcher deployment gate.
- Deterministic fictional fixture catalog and staging/deployment/security runbooks.
- OpenAPI/generated-client, registry, automated test, and verification updates.
- CI coverage for deterministic artifact drift, inventory/schema unit checks, the reversible migration rehearsal, existing API-client drift checks, and the mocked Playwright journey.
- Final review hardening covers serialized audit ownership and lifecycle mutations, plan-controlled task and project status/schedules, sibling-plan activation that preserves the first start and longest aggregate deadline, canonical execution/case/task/project traceability, audit-linked environment enforcement under the owning plan lock and explicit case-derived role-under-test capture, submitted non-duplicate canonical report targets with transactional chain/cycle rejection, reporter-authored evidence protected from administrative rewrites and required-field removal, terminal-execution and finalized-report immutability for every actor, failed/blocked and terminal-only strong-evidence alignment, universally enforced and transactionally rechecked `ready_for_retest` state plus a fresh passing retest from the current cycle before every verification including reopened reports, an explicit Spanish administrative-exception workflow with immutable justification and approval provenance, and durable production evidence storage in a mounted private subtree denied by the public raw-file route and enforced by a fail-closed release guard.

## Security and privacy

Intern reports are private by reporter; backend authorization protects reports and evidence. The intern cannot set authoritative severity/priority, broaden roles, activate, close, or see other users' private reports. Attachments are validated and privately stored; heavy video is linked. Production mutation, real recipients, live payments, secrets, publication, inventory mutation, and music delivery are prohibited.

## Migration and rollback

Apply the registered base migration `2026-08-21_studio_internship_audit.sql`, completion-exception control, and historical-failure gate in manifest order; they are rerunnable and leave legacy feedback untouched. After stopping new writes and exporting retained audit records, roll back the historical gate, then the guarded completion-exception migration, then the paired base rollback. Release preflight must verify manifest checksums and ancestry.

## Test plan

Use the exact command/result table from `docs/internships/studio-audit/TEST-RESULTS.md`. The final tree passes 2,443 backend examples, 1,676 web tests across 167 suites, the production build and initial-bundle budget, the lint error gate, all 10 targeted Playwright combinations, and the disposable API lifecycle (including audit-plan environment matching on linked report creation/update/submission, case-derived role-under-test capture, canonical duplicate-target enforcement, reporter-evidence ownership/completeness, concurrent reopen/retest serialization, rejection of generic audit-project status/schedule overrides, sibling-plan schedule aggregation, plan-controlled task due dates, immutable administrative-exception provenance, old-retest rejection after reopening, and fresh current-cycle retest acceptance). Repository quality with zero critical/error findings, OpenAPI, registry, type checking, migration, mobile, isolated staging health/CORS, and inactive-draft authorization checks also pass. The feature-audit pending-disposition gate and missing provider credentials/dispatcher remain visible.

## Deployment gates

- Supply Stewart Moreira's verified production party ID and email only at approved draft-creation runtime; do not commit those identifiers or create a duplicate account.
- Review/approve least-privilege module grants and notification recipients.
- Connect and verify an approved external outbox dispatcher/digest schedule, or explicitly approve in-app-only notifications.
- Review the integrated `TDF-mobile` generated-client commit `dfb4bc5b64f957e93d5deab705aa971d20268f62` (mobile PRs #30, #31, and #32); the parent repository points to that exact remote commit.
- Review the deployed isolated staging topology, synthetic data, and test transports.
- Review the staging inactive draft; the complete intern/admin lifecycle and rollback have disposable local automation, while physical-device and external-provider staging checks remain manual.
- Obtain separate approval for activation/notification.

## Draft-task preview

Link `docs/internships/studio-audit/DRAFT-PREVIEW.md`, the Spanish guide, inventory summary, case counts, schedule, permission proposal, notification behavior, and completion gates.

## External actions

Branch creation, commits, pushes, PR creation, isolated staging deployment, and inactive staging draft creation were authorized. The API/web/database are deployed and the staging draft remains hidden and unassigned with zero assignment notifications. No production deployment, GitHub issue, task activation, assignment to Stewart, or real notification is authorized. Confirm each remaining gate separately.

## Scope

Adds a repository-native persona-based testing program derived from the implemented backend, web, mobile, route, permission, schema, test, documentation, and prior-audit surfaces.

- 26 deterministic fictional personas across 17 risk-ranked epics and 78 complete-lifecycle stories
- JSON scenario/persona definitions, generated Markdown specifications, and a 78-row CSV traceability matrix
- opt-in, non-production-only Haskell persona seeding with runtime-only credentials
- Playwright browser E2E, axe checks, responsive/cross-browser projects, failure artifacts, and CI gating
- refreshed feature/route/API/role/platform inventory and truthful mobile web fallbacks
- consolidated findings, permission/security assessment, parity report, release backlog, coverage gaps, and future human-testing protocol

The mobile submodule points to pushed commit `cff51d76233ea1d81f4e6ae7b30789cd9aaf83ee` on `diegueins680/TDF-mobile:feat/persona-testing-program-20260821`.

## Personas and epics covered

The catalog includes visitors, fans/customers, independent and multi-role artists, collaborators, producers, A&R, teachers/students, interns, reception/studio/maintenance staff, webmaster/admin/accounting, venues, buyers/sellers, event organizers, Live Sessions, Domo, and label/distribution clients. It covers all 17 requested epics from identity and discovery through commerce, payments, operations, administration, accessibility, and cross-epic reconciliation.

Five stories have partial automated or direct-observation evidence. The other 73 remain explicitly `specified-not-executed`; no partial result is represented as a complete lifecycle pass.

## Confirmed findings by severity

- Blocker: 0
- Critical: 0
- High: 6 — PT-001, PT-002, PT-003, PT-004, PT-008, PT-011
- Medium: 4 — PT-005, PT-007, PT-009, PT-010
- Low: 1 — PT-006

Implemented fixes cover PT-001/002/003/005/009/010/011. PT-004 remains a 40-endpoint product/security disposition gate; PT-008 keeps incomplete DDEX delivery concealed; PT-007 requires advisory-level dependency triage; PT-006 is a one-time non-reproducing timeout retained for monitoring.

## Important security fix

The PostgreSQL-backed PER-02 journey confirmed that logout expired the browser cookie without deactivating the corresponding `api_token`, so a preserved pre-logout cookie remained replayable. Logout now independently parses bearer and cookie credentials, deduplicates them, deactivates every matching active token, and always expires the cookie.

Post-fix evidence: login produced one active PER-02 token; logout returned 200; stale-cookie replay returned `null`; the database reported zero active PER-02 tokens. Raw tokens and the runtime-only password were redacted and the disposable database was destroyed.

## Test environments

- Base: `origin/main` `560ac9954b655ba8aa719963a2c890110b74a232`
- Local isolated worktree only; staging and production untouched
- macOS 14.7.7, Node 24.8.0, npm 11.6.0, Stack 3.7.1, GHC 9.10.3
- Disposable PostgreSQL 16 cluster on a loopback-only socket/port
- Browser mocks for public/auth flows; Chromium desktop/phone/tablet and critical Firefox/WebKit
- Existing React Native Jest coverage; no Detox simulator execution
- No payment, OAuth, email, notification, social, WhatsApp, ticket-delivery, or distribution provider contacted

## Commands and results

- `REQUIRE_STACK=1 npm run quality:backend` — 2,420 examples, 0 failures
- `npm run quality:ui` — 162 suites/1,652 tests; lint 0 errors/93 baseline warnings; typecheck/build passed
- `REQUIRE_MOBILE_WORKSPACE=1 npm run quality:mobile` — 49 suites/256 tests; lint/typecheck passed
- `npm run test:e2e:web` — 15 passed, 2 expected project-specific skips; zero serious/critical axe findings in instrumented states
- `npm run quality:repo` — passed; formal audit 8,676 findings, 0 errors, 307 warnings
- `npm run test:persona-program` — 3/3 tests; 26 personas, 78 stories, 17 epics
- `REQUIRE_MOBILE_WORKSPACE=1 npm run generate:api` — web/mobile clients regenerated
- `npm run typecheck:ui` and `npm --prefix tdf-mobile run typecheck` — passed
- `npm run generate:features && npm run audit:features` — passed with 137 features, 156 web routes, 38 mobile routes
- `ALLOW_PENDING_FEATURE_DISPOSITIONS=1 npm run generate:feature-audit-reports` — packet generated for 548 endpoints and 3,014 role/action/platform rows

## Remaining failures and known limitations

- Default feature-audit generation intentionally remains red while 40 endpoints lack explicit interface/security disposition.
- Targeted HLint reports existing hints outside the changed seed/logout lines; Ormolu proposes broad legacy whole-file rewrites. No unrelated formatting sweep is included.
- npm install reported 6 moderate/6 high root and 4 moderate/35 high mobile advisories; runtime reachability is not yet triaged.
- One mobile checkout test exceeded its timeout once during a cold run; isolated and full reruns passed without retry or timeout inflation.
- Firefox/WebKit cover only the critical auth slice; automated axe covers representative public auth/directory/ticket states, not the full application.
- No iOS Detox, Android native E2E, full keyboard/screen-reader session, large-data/performance soak, provider certification, or real participant study was performed.

## Migration and rollback considerations

No schema migration is introduced. The backend's forward Persistent/catalog/trials migration path and persona seed completed twice against disposable PostgreSQL with identical counts: 25 account personas, 25 active bcrypt credentials, 47 active canonical role assignments across 21 roles, zero duplicate reserved emails, and zero pre-login persona tokens. The 26th persona is the intentional unauthenticated visitor.

Rollback is ordinary code/config reversal; reverting the logout fix would reopen PT-011. Standalone domain migration scripts and rollback paths were not executed by this program and remain release gates.

## Security and privacy safeguards

- all personas are explicitly fictional and use the reserved `persona.test` domain
- persona seeding is disabled by default and requires a local/test runtime, an explicit feature flag, and a 16+ character runtime-only password
- fixtures match reserved emails/credentials, never display names, and create no public directory projection
- provider workers/calls were disabled; no real account, recipient, payment method, ticket, release, or public content was created
- browser artifacts are ignored/CI-retained and failure-only; committed evidence contains no credentials, tokens, payment data, or real PII
- the disposable database and token-bearing cookie files were permanently removed after execution

## Manual and external gates

Provider sandboxes, refunds/reconciliation, email/notification delivery, OAuth, DDEX partner certification, staging data, production configuration, and genuine human usability sessions require separate authorization or credentials. No SUS, UMUX-Lite, NPS, testimony, emotion, or participant score is fabricated in this PR.

title: [codex] reconcile materialized provider entity aliases
body:
## Summary

PR #170 was merged at `2233005535d663d88d8d930fcc629cf68419b6cc` before its exact automated review identified one remaining P1: a later structured-provider refresh could create duplicate venue/artist entities because materialization stores deterministic `event-research:*` aliases until native provider entity IDs are known.

This follow-up blocks deployment/materialization until that gap is closed.

## Changes

- reconcile a provider's native venue ID to a same-provider synthetic venue alias only when normalized name, city, and confirmed country resolve uniquely
- reconcile a provider's native artist ID to a same-provider synthetic artist alias only when normalized identity resolves uniquely
- abort the discovery transaction on ambiguous synthetic identity instead of guessing or creating duplicates
- retain both synthetic and native external references for audit and replay
- document the alias transition
- remove one duplicated `DEFAULT_LOCALE=es` line reintroduced into `main` by the concurrent #169 merge; this restores the existing CI invariant and is isolated in its own commit

title: [codex] add idempotent event research materialization
body:
## Summary

Production can research and approve event candidates, but it has no safe way to materialize an approved candidate as a TDF event. The generic event write is not idempotent and cannot atomically preserve the candidate link, provider references, related entities, and ingestion audit.

This draft adds the minimum materialization path required for the approved pilot. It does not deploy or write production data.

## Changes

- add strict-admin `POST /social-events/event-research/candidates/{candidateId}/materialize`
- require an explicit open materialization run and lock the pilot, run, and candidate rows
- enforce approved pilot plus high-confidence/draft/official-sale/start/venue/city/lineup gates
- allow a confirmed start with `end_time = null`; only an explicit unsupported blocker prevents materialization
- resolve existing provider references and normalized venue/artist identities; reject ambiguity instead of guessing
- create only missing venues and unclaimed artists, leaving unverified profile data null
- atomically create/reuse the event, external references, candidate link, and immutable change audit
- make replay return the original event/change without rewriting manual event fields
- add OpenAPI, generated UI types/client support, tests, and ingestion documentation

## Production read-only preflight

- approved pilot: 20 candidates total
- selected batch: 8 high-confidence draft candidates
- all 8 currently have no event link and no external event reference
- secondary duplicate scan found no matching existing events
- exactly one active published `concert` event type
- exact entity scan indicates 4 venues and 11 unclaimed artists would be new
- 12 medium-confidence/review candidates remain untouched
- no production writes were performed

## Verification

- focused backend research tests: 12 examples, 0 failures
- full backend suite before the final non-overlapping `main` rebase: 2,305 examples, 0 failures
- OpenAPI client regeneration: clean
- UI TypeScript check on current `main`: passed
- production release tests on current `main`: 43/43
- CI pipeline tests on current `main`: 14/14
- `git diff --check`: passed

A second full backend compile after rebasing onto current `main` stopped because the local APFS volume had only 134 MiB free (`No space left on device`) while compiling an unrelated module changed by `main`. The rebase had no overlap with this PR's eight files; GitHub CI should provide the clean-environment confirmation.

## Rollout and rollback

1. Review and merge this PR.
2. Build/deploy through the existing production release process under separate authorization.
3. Create a dedicated materialization run.
4. Materialize the eight candidates in small batches, replay each request, then close/checkpoint the run.
5. Do not auto-delete created data on rollback; roll back application code and keep audit/history for reconciliation.

No migration is required: existing candidate links, external references, change actions, and unique dedupe keys cover the operation.

body:
## Situación inicial

La PR #160 ya integró en `main` el editor enriquecido de perfiles profesionales. Su evidencia pública
estaba completa, pero faltaba una captura reproducible del flujo autenticado en web y Expo Web. Al
automatizar ese gate aparecieron dos fallos reales en Expo Web: el bootstrap intentaba usar
`SecureStore` antes del almacenamiento compatible con navegador y el deep link inicial reenviaba la
URL actual en bucle.

Este follow-up parte de `main` en `c31d979b8` y apunta al commit móvil `5a1e1b0` de
[TDF-mobile#24](https://github.com/diegueins680/TDF-mobile/pull/24).

## Decisiones y funciones implementadas

- El capturador visual acepta `all`, `web-managed` y `mobile-managed`, además de una instalación local
  configurable de Playwright/Chromium.
- La sesión, el perfil multi-profesión, tarifas, idiomas, portafolio y dos ciudades son fixtures
  sintéticos interceptados localmente. `synthetic-visual-token` no es una credencial de TDF ni sale
  del origen local.
- La captura exige el round trip del nombre administrado antes de guardar evidencia y audita las dos
  superficies autenticadas con Axe.
- Los `Select` del editor web tienen asociaciones `InputLabel`/`labelId`; los switches móviles tienen
  nombres accesibles; el contraste de navegación y del indicador API offline queda corregido.
- Expo Web usa almacenamiento compatible con navegador sin depender de `SecureStore`, y conserva la
  sesión en memoria si el storage no está disponible.
- El manejador de deep links normaliza rutas y no navega de nuevo cuando el navegador ya abrió el
  destino actual.
- Los cinco conjuntos nuevos del fixture tienen decisiones explícitas en la auditoría de catálogos;
  ninguno se presenta como autoridad editorial o de seguridad.

## Esquema, API y compatibilidad

No hay DDL, backfill, endpoint ni contrato OpenAPI nuevo. El cambio reutiliza el perfil, sesión,
taxonomías y navegación existentes. El rollback consiste en revertir este commit raíz y el commit
móvil `5a1e1b0`; no hay datos que revertir.

## Seguridad y privacidad

- No se incluyen secretos, PII, perfiles reales, coordenadas residenciales, verificaciones ni
  transacciones simuladas.
- Todas las solicitudes autenticadas de la evidencia son interceptadas; no contactan producción.
- La captura anónima sigue comprobando el `401` esperado de sesión y el reporte final conserva cero
  errores inesperados de navegador.

## Verificación ejecutada

- Web completo previo del mismo cambio: 151 suites, 1.610 pruebas, 0 fallos.
- Head exacto: 23 pruebas web focalizadas, 0 fallos; build de producción con 12.386 módulos y
  406.718 bytes gzip de JS inicial.
- Móvil exacto: 22 pruebas focalizadas, typecheck y lint, todo verde.
- Suite móvil conjunta local: 52/53 suites y 271/272 pruebas; el único timeout de `TicketCheckout`
  pasa 14/14 aislado. No se debilitó ni amplió el timeout.
- GitHub CI del head completo: build, UI, móvil, repositorio, catálogos, contratos, migraciones,
  quality gate, Cloudflare Pages y Vercel pasan; los jobs backend/API no afectados se omiten por scope.
- Auditoría de catálogos y `git diff --check`: pass.
- Evidencia visual: 8 PNG, 7 superficies Axe, 189 reglas aprobadas, 0 violaciones, 8 comprobaciones
  incompletas para revisión humana y 0 errores inesperados de navegador.

Detalle reproducible: [verification-evidence.md](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/blob/feat/music-directory-authenticated-visuals-20260818/docs/music-directory/verification-evidence.md).

## Evidencia visual

![Editor web autenticado](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/blob/feat/music-directory-authenticated-visuals-20260818/docs/music-directory/screenshots/web-desktop-profile-editor.png?raw=1)

## Riesgos y gates externos

- VoiceOver/TalkBack, binarios iOS/Android y hardware real siguen siendo gates manuales.

title: fix: retain DDEX migration-only rollback column
body:
## What changed

- retains `ddex_partner.allowed_versions` in the Persistent migration model as a `MigrationOnly` field
- preserves PR #164's governed `text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'` rollback-evidence contract
- removes the legacy field from normal DDEX partner records and application writes; canonical version policy remains in `ddex_partner_standard_version`

## Root cause

The governed DDEX cutover intentionally keeps `allowed_versions` as empty rollback evidence. Removing the field entirely made Persistent propose the unsafe operation `DROP COLUMN ddex_partner.allowed_versions`. PR #164 retained the column, but exposed it as an application field. This resolution combines both protections: the database migration model retains the column while generated application records and writers do not.

## Impact

Persistent can inspect the schema without proposing the destructive drop. Normal DDEX partner APIs and writes remain canonical and cannot mutate the legacy evidence column. Production continues through PR #164's checksum-pinned reviewed SQL lane; the production entrypoint explicitly disables inferred Persistent migrations after applying that bundle.

## Conflict resolution

Merged current `main` (`cc7d64c1f20e2626df53ef32a0e4ee142c0a220b`) into the PR and resolved the overlapping DDEX model in favor of:

- PR #164's documented empty-array default and compatibility migration
- PR #165's `MigrationOnly` isolation
- removal of the now-unneeded writer argument

Exact head: `7684fc760c9bb7f5605c6a8d13413e0665f7c0f5`.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- production release tests: 43/43 passed
- CI pipeline tests: 14/14 passed
- dedicated DDEX compatibility migration test passed against PostgreSQL 16 in Docker
- the harness now mirrors `fly.toml`; its shell syntax and focused local suites pass
- protected GitHub CI [run 32144823574](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/32144823574) passed on the exact head above, including the complete backend suite and idempotent production-schema migration verification

## Rollout safety

After protected CI and renewed approval, merge with the normal merge method. Continue through the guarded reviewed-migration release lane; do not enable inferred Persistent migrations globally.

title: fix(db): make automatic migrations fail closed
body:
## Summary

- retain `ddex_partner.allowed_versions` as empty rollback evidence instead of letting Persistent infer a destructive drop
- preflight every Persistent model migration before any schema or seed write and reject the complete unsafe plan
- register an idempotent, fail-closed migration that changes the legacy default to an empty array
- package the checksum-pinned production SQL manifest into the backend image and apply it automatically before startup
- keep `RUN_MIGRATIONS=false` in production so Persistent-inferred DDL cannot become a second schema authority
- run the real production entrypoint twice against the fully cut-over PostgreSQL fixture and require an unchanged schema fingerprint

## Production context

Event discovery is enabled on both Fly Machines with automatic publication disabled. A guarded `RUN_MIGRATIONS=true` canary on revision `591abfacddd8a3acfbe117421efe65382fa73252` first exposed an inferred destructive DDEX column drop. The first CI follow-up then exposed a non-destructive-looking but invalid Persistent constraint/index collision plus extensive unreviewed type/default drift.

This PR therefore separates the authorities:

- `AUTO_APPLY_PRODUCTION_MIGRATIONS=true` runs only reviewed SQL from `scripts/production-migrations.json`, protected by checksums, `tdf_schema_migration`, an advisory lock and the full schema verifier.
- `RUN_MIGRATIONS=false` prevents model-inferred DDL in the production process.
- The backend starts only after all pending reviewed migrations and schema verification succeed.

The currently deployed fleet has not been changed by this PR. Pre-write snapshot: `vs_n2LkNLnjox1SlaxwXnM8o2` (identifier only; no credentials).

## Verification

- `stack build --fast --test --no-run-tests`
- `npm run test:production-release` — 43 passed
- `npm run test:ci-pipeline` — 14 passed
- `npm run audit:catalog-lists` — passed with the reviewed allowlist
- shell syntax and `git diff --check` — passed
- PostgreSQL forward/idempotency/schema-fingerprint test is wired into `backend-quality`
- Docker image construction is validated by the Build Image workflow because the local Docker daemon was unavailable

## Rollout

1. Require all CI checks and exact human review while the PR remains draft.
2. Merge through branch protection and build an immutable image for the merge SHA.
3. Create a fresh production snapshot and run the release dry-run/preflight.
4. Apply migration 42 through the guarded release lane.
5. Deploy one canary with `AUTO_APPLY_PRODUCTION_MIGRATIONS=true`, `RUN_MIGRATIONS=false`, discovery staged off and auto-publication off.
6. Verify checksum ledger, schema, health, image revision and no-op startup migration logs; then roll the second Machine.
7. Re-enable discovery after fleet verification, keep auto-publication off, and verify the next discovery run.
8. Restore the snapshot or use the migration-specific rollback if any schema, health, authorization or discovery gate fails.

title: feat(directory): enable rich professional profile editing
body:
## Situación inicial

Este PR continúa sobre `main` en `a91e68753` (Directorio y Clasificados ya integrado por #152). El
esquema normalizado almacenaba experiencia, créditos, multimedia, tarifas, detalle profesional,
idiomas y varias áreas de servicio, pero el writer sólo aceptaba el perfil básico, la proyección de
manager no alcanzaba para reconstruir un editor y web/móvil no permitían editar esos datos. Idiomas
tampoco formaban parte del bundle público del directorio.

Auditoría basada en código, SQL, OpenAPI y pruebas: [rich-profile-audit-2026-08-17.md](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/blob/feat/music-directory-rich-profiles-20260817/docs/music-directory/rich-profile-audit-2026-08-17.md).

## Decisiones y funciones implementadas

- Se amplía `directory_profile` y sus relaciones existentes; no se crea otro perfil, catálogo,
  ubicación ni subsistema comercial.
- `DirectoryProfileUpsert` conserva los campos históricos y añade DTO cerrados para experiencia,
  créditos, equipo, disponibilidad, tarifas, portafolio, enlaces, detalles por profesión e
  instrumento, idiomas y múltiples áreas.
- Una cuenta puede crear/editar varios perfiles, siempre mediante un grant activo y explícito de
  `directory_profile_manager`; las profesiones públicas siguen sin conceder capacidades internas.
- `GET /directory/profiles`, creación, actualización, transición de estado y replay idempotente
  comparten la misma proyección privada exacta.
- El writer valida conjuntos sin duplicados, jerarquía país/región/ciudad/metro, una sola ubicación
  primaria, rangos, enums y URLs HTTP(S) o same-origin sin credenciales.
- Portafolio/enlaces históricos se normalizan al DTO cerrado al leer, sin reescribir el JSON fuente.
  Las nuevas escrituras se normalizan antes de persistir.
- La edición genera auditoría de intención sin copiar biografía, créditos, enlaces u otro contenido
  del perfil al log.
- Web y móvil incorporan crear/editar perfiles ricos, múltiples profesiones, idiomas, ciudades,
  modalidad, tarifas, portafolio y redes. Áreas regionales/nacionales que el selector aún no edita
  se conservan en el round trip.
- OpenAPI es canónico y ambos clientes fueron regenerados. El cambio móvil actualiza el draft
  [TDF-mobile#24](https://github.com/diegueins680/TDF-mobile/pull/24) hasta `64d7878`.

## Esquema, compatibilidad y migración

No hay DDL ni backfill nuevo: todas las columnas, claves e índices requeridos ya estaban desplegados.
En un `PUT`, omitir un campo rico conserva su valor; string/array vacío o `clearRates=true` expresa
borrado deliberado. El payload histórico sigue siendo válido y conserva detalles, idiomas y áreas
secundarias. Cambiar entre sujeto personal y organizacional requiere reconciliación auditada y no se
permite desde el editor ordinario.

Rollback: desplegar el artefacto anterior o revertir estos cinco commits raíz y los dos commits móviles. Los
datos ricos permanecen compatibles con writers anteriores; no hay SQL destructivo que revertir.

## Seguridad y privacidad

- Ningún writer acepta dirección exacta ni coordenadas residenciales.
- Las coordenadas públicas creadas por esta ruta provienen sólo del centroide de ciudad.
- DTO públicos y de manager tienen `additionalProperties: false`; la proyección pública no contiene
  Party, capacidades, PII, tokens ni datos administrativos.
- URLs con `userinfo`, protocolo relativo, controles, espacios internos o backslash se rechazan.
- Permisos de autorización y profesiones públicas permanecen en dominios separados.

## Verificación ejecutada

- `stack build --fast`: 141 módulos enlazados.
- Hspec/QuickCheck dirigido: 15 ejemplos, 0 fallos; siete propiedades con 100 casos cada una.
- PostgreSQL 16/API: pass completo de restart, backfill/rollback, creación/replay, segundo perfil,
  detalle rico, dos áreas, compatibilidad histórica, normalización de media, privacidad, auditoría,
  casos negativos y el resto de invariantes del directorio.
- Contrato OpenAPI y auditor formal: pass, 0 errores.
- Web: typecheck pass; Jest dirigido 9/9.
- Móvil: Jest dirigido local 5/5; `mobile-quality` en CI limpio pasó lint, typecheck y la suite
  completa después de `npm ci`.
- GitHub CI: `quality`, backend, web, móvil, contratos API, auditoría de catálogos, instalación segura,
  Datadog y Cloudflare Pages pasaron en `8db5ffff`; el PR móvil también está verde en `64d7878`.
- `git diff --check`: pass. No se debilitaron suites.

Detalle reproducible: [verification-evidence.md](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/blob/feat/music-directory-rich-profiles-20260817/docs/music-directory/verification-evidence.md).

## Evidencia visual

Estas capturas sintéticas documentan las superficies públicas heredadas de #152; no contienen datos
de producción. La captura específica del editor autenticado nuevo permanece como gate manual.

![Búsqueda web](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/blob/feat/music-directory-rich-profiles-20260817/docs/music-directory/screenshots/web-desktop-search-list.png?raw=1)

![Mapa web](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/blob/feat/music-directory-rich-profiles-20260817/docs/music-directory/screenshots/web-desktop-search-map.png?raw=1)

![Directorio móvil](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/blob/feat/music-directory-rich-profiles-20260817/docs/music-directory/screenshots/mobile-expo-directory-results.png?raw=1)

## Riesgos y gates externos

- Ambos PRs están verdes y permanecen en draft para revisión humana.
- Capturar el editor web y móvil autenticado con fixtures sintéticos; revisar VoiceOver/TalkBack en
  hardware/emulador.
- Firma/distribución móvil, entrega real de email/push y cualquier despliegue requieren credenciales
  e infraestructura; no se simularon.
- Revisión jurídica de menores, moderación y jurisdicciones sigue siendo un gate de release.

## Validación y despliegue exactos

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
(cd tdf-hq && stack build --fast)
node scripts/test-music-directory-contract.mjs
node scripts/audit-formal-methods.mjs --fail-on error
./scripts/test-music-directory-migration.sh
(cd tdf-hq-ui && npm ci && npm run generate:api && npm run typecheck && npm test -- --runTestsByPath src/pages/DirectoryManagePage.test.ts)
(cd tdf-mobile && npm ci && npm run generate:api && npm run typecheck && npm test -- --runTestsByPath src/features/directory/profileForm.test.ts)
```

Orden de release: revisar/mergear primero TDF-mobile#24, desplegar backend compatible, desplegar web y
recién después generar binarios móviles firmados. No ejecutar migración SQL para este PR. Smoke test:
crear dos perfiles con una cuenta, editar profesiones/idiomas/dos ciudades, publicar uno, verificar la
vista pública anónima y confirmar que el DTO no contiene PII ni ubicación exacta.

title: fix(events): make official end and duration optional
body:
## Resultado

Permite crear y actualizar eventos sin fin oficial ni duración confirmada. El inicio sigue siendo obligatorio y un fin explícito debe ser posterior al inicio.

## Cambios

- social_event.end_time pasa a nullable con una migración idempotente y una restricción validada para el orden temporal.
- El rollback se niega si existen fines nulos, evitando pérdida o invención de datos.
- OpenAPI acepta eventEnd omitido o null y se regeneran los clientes web y móvil.
- El panel web y la app móvil ofrecen Fin por confirmar y no generan una duración implícita.
- La reconciliación de discovery no marca finalizado un evento sin fin confirmado.
- La verificación de release exige la columna nullable y la restricción validada.
- El submódulo móvil apunta al commit 28f8837f8abf1574749e0faec669de3fb3a6813b.

## Pruebas

- Backend Haskell: compilación completa; 3 pruebas validateEventTimeRange; 238 pruebas FromJSON.
- Web: 5 pruebas de creación colaborativa; typecheck completo.
- Móvil: 53 pruebas focalizadas de creación, tarjetas y mapeo.
- Release: 39 pruebas del contrato de release.
- PostgreSQL 16: aplicación doble, null aceptado, orden inválido rechazado, rollback protegido, rollback seguro y reaplicación.
- OpenAPI: clientes web y móvil regenerados desde el contrato.

## Riesgos y mitigaciones

- La validación de la nueva restricción fallará si existen datos históricos con end_time menor o igual a start_time. El despliegue debe comprobar esos registros antes de aplicar la migración.
- El rollback requiere resolver primero cualquier evento con end_time nulo; no inventa duraciones.
- Producción no fue desplegada ni modificada por este PR.

## Despliegue

1. Verificar que no existan filas con end_time no nulo y end_time menor o igual a start_time.
2. Ejecutar el flujo normal de release; la migración registrada es 2026-08-17_social_event_optional_end.
3. Confirmar la verificación de esquema y probar create/update con eventEnd omitido, null y explícito.
4. Materializar después los candidatos de investigación bloqueados por fin no confirmado, conservando el piloto y sus reglas de publicación.

## Summary

- derive the image `BUILD_TIME` deterministically from the exact source commit timestamp for push, manual, and reusable workflow runs
- reject empty or malformed source SHA/build-time arguments while constructing the runtime image
- add CI regression coverage so unsupported GitHub contexts cannot silently restore stale `/version` metadata

## Root cause

The manual Build Image run had no `github.event.head_commit`, and `github.run_started_at` did not resolve to a supported context value. Docker therefore received an empty `BUILD_TIME`; the backend correctly rejected it and fell back to its older compiled timestamp.

## Verification

- `npm run test:ci-pipeline` — 13/13 passed
- `npm run test:production-release` — 39/39 passed
- deterministic metadata smoke check — `2026-08-17T09:21:17Z`
- `docker buildx build --check ... -f tdf-hq/Dockerfile.runtime .` — no warnings
- `git diff --check` — passed

## Rollout boundary

This PR changes only image-build metadata. It does not modify database migrations, runtime schema, application contracts, or feature flags. Merging it must not be treated as authorization to deploy unrelated changes already present on `main`.

title: feat(events): add auditable research ingestion pilot
body:
## Summary

- add a strict-admin, evidence-backed event research queue with idempotent runs, checkpoints, candidate upserts, and append-only change audit
- enforce the unapproved pilot limit of 20 active candidates in PostgreSQL, including safe retry and discard/replace behavior
- persist explicit event timezones and expose official manual web sources without allowing the structured-feed cron to scrape them
- document the workflow, add OpenAPI/generated client support, and include the 2026-08-16 Sunday reconciliation checkpoint with exactly 20 unique Ecuador candidates

## Operational result

- production was inspected read-only; health is OK and the deployed commit is `d10e7cdf`
- no pilot approval indicator exists, the attached admin browser redirected to login, and the deployed schema lacks the required audit contract
- no production event, entity, source, checkpoint, or approval was written; nothing was published or deployed
- Passline presented Cloudflare and Feel The Tickets presented Queue-it; neither control was bypassed

## Safety and idempotency

- every new route requires strict admin access
- candidate upsert key is `(provider, external_id)` and the server computes the content hash
- exact retries create neither duplicate candidates nor duplicate change entries
- closed runs reject material changes; checkpoints and terminal timestamps are durable
- database locking enforces an accumulated maximum of 20 active pilot candidates until an explicit append-audited approval
- candidates never create or publish `social_event` records
- imported/source-managed fields are recorded so later materialization can preserve manual edits
- all official HTML/web source registry entries are forced disabled for cron ingestion

## Verification

- `./scripts/test-event-research-ingestion-migration.sh` — source seeds, pilot cap, retry idempotency, discard/replace, rollback, and reapply passed
- focused Hspec — 5 examples passed for candidate validation, material hash stability, timezone/evidence requirements, and disabled HTTPS web sources
- UI Jest — 147 suites / 1,593 tests passed
- UI TypeScript typecheck passed
- ESLint passed for every modified UI source file
- OpenAPI client generation passed
- production release manifest tests — 37 passed
- catalog-list governance audit passed with the mobile submodule initialized
- the new backend module compiled successfully

The repository's current `main` full backend build is independently blocked by pre-existing missing `Data.List.foldl'` imports in `ServerRadio`, `ServerProposals`, `SocialEventsHandlers`, `Server`, and `Cron`. Temporary local imports were used only to execute the focused Hspec suite and were reverted; this PR does not mix those unrelated fixes.

## Risks and rollout

- apply `tdf-hq/sql/2026-08-16_event_research_ingestion.sql` before deploying code that serves the new routes
- review the 20-candidate checkpoint before any authenticated replay
- do not call the approval endpoint until Diego explicitly approves the accumulated pilot
- event materialization/publication and first-class promoter/organizer/ticket-seller entities remain follow-up work; evidence is retained in the candidate payload meanwhile
- the reverse migration is provided, but it removes research queue data; capture a backup before rollback after real ingestion

This PR is intentionally draft. It does not authorize a migration, deployment, production write, pilot approval, or publication.
